papers.title: A physics-based-preconditioned quasi-Newton solver for energy- and momentum-conserving implicit hybrid particle-in-cell simulations
papers.abstract: Explicit hybrid particle-in-cell (PIC) schemes, with kinetic ions and fluid electrons, accumulate numerical heating over long simulations and are unstable to finite-grid instabilities. Energy-conserving implicit integration removes heating and instabilities, but may be inefficient due to the need of nonlinear iteration. We present a fast quasi-Newton solver for an implicit hybrid-PIC formulation. The nonlinear residual employs the electric field and electron pressure as nonlinear unknowns, and nonlinearly eliminates particles. The formulation is strictly energy conserving and, on Cartesian meshes, also momentum conserving. The nonlinear iteration is efficiently performed with a quasi-Newton solver that replaces the true Jacobian with an approximate one without spoiling conservation properties upon convergence. The approximate Jacobian replaces the particle ion linear response with an analytical mass matrix that is local and requires minimal storage. This approximate Jacobian is efficiently inverted with a physics-based multigrid preconditioner, adapted from Hall MHD. We verify the scheme linearly with whistler, kinetic Alfv\'en, and cylindrical normal modes, and nonlinearly with the GEM reconnection challenge. On GEM, explicit integration needs a forty-times-smaller time step, and nine times the wall-clock time, to reach an energy conservation comparable to that of the implicit solver. We apply the method to the simulation of a three-dimensional field-reversed configuration formation by external coils.
papers.intro:
Field-reversed configurations (FRCs) are compact, high-beta plasmas in which the ion gyroradius is comparable to the gradient scale lengths, so that ion kinetic effects influence stability and transport, while formation, merging, and compression unfold over many Alfvén transit times [30, 5]. Helion Energy’s pulsed approach, in which FRCs are formed, merged, and magnetically compressed, is a demanding example [4]. Hybrid particle-in-cell (PIC) methods, which treat the ions kinetically and the electrons as a fluid closed by a generalized Ohm’s law, resolve the ion scales without the electron-plasma-frequency and light-speed constraints of fully kinetic PIC, and are widely used for such problems and for space and laboratory plasmas more broadly [23, 34, 17, 6].

Despite its asymptotic reductions, hybrid PIC still faces a restrictive explicit time-step stability limit. The Hall term in Ohm’s law supports whistler waves whose frequency grows as k2k^{2} at short wavelengths, requiring Δ​t∝Δ​x2\Delta t\propto\Delta x^{2} [18, 10]. With explicit integration, halving the mesh spacing reduces the stable time step fourfold, and the sub-cycling typically used to relieve the constraint accumulates error over long simulations. Explicit hybrid schemes typically conserve neither energy nor momentum and, under certain conditions, are subject to the finite-grid instability [25]. Its growth rate is not arrested by mesh refinement, resulting in secular numerical heating. Fully implicit, energy-conserving integration removes stability constraints and secular heating [28, 21], and lets the time step follow the ion dynamics. Its wall-clock-time performance then rests on the cost of the nonlinear solver. In a Jacobian-free Newton–Krylov (JFNK) method [20], every Krylov iteration re-evaluates the nonlinear residual and therefore re-advances all particles, so that its cost is approximately proportional to the number of Krylov iterations, which grows with the condition number of the Jacobian unless the linear system is preconditioned. Even with efficient preconditioning, JFNK still requires a particle push per Krylov iteration, which can remain too expensive in practice and motivates using a quasi–Newton approach that employs a suitable approximation to the Jacobian that avoids the particles altogether, e.g. by using an analytical mass-matrix approximation of the particle response [2, 1].

Stanier et al. combined the implicit midpoint rule, nonlinear elimination of the particles, and JFNK into a fully implicit hybrid algorithm that conserves energy and, on Cartesian meshes, momentum [28]. For hyperbolic PDEs, physics-based preconditioning is the established route to manageable Krylov counts that grow slowly with the time step [20]. In implicit MHD, approximate block factorizations reduce the coupled system to Schur complements that multigrid inverts efficiently [9, 11]. In implicit PIC, moment-based preconditioners play the same role for the kinetically enslaved JFNK solve, first in the electrostatic model [13] and then in the Darwin model [14]. Most directly relevant here, the fully implicit Hall-MHD solver in [12] isolates the stiff electron block, poses it for the vector potential, and relaxes it with a coupled smoother that inverts a local approximation at each node while the multigrid residual retains the exact discrete curl–curl operator.

Our focus is to extend this Hall-MHD preconditioner to kinetic-ion hybrid PIC. As in [12], its field block couples the electric-field update to an auxiliary curl–curl variable, and it retains the Hall rotation, resistive and hyper-resistive damping, and electron convection. Beyond the reference, we adapt it to the hybrid PIC context by employing a local approximation of the ion linear response via analytical mass matrices, discussed below. As in [12], relaxation is by a block-Jacobi smoother whose nodal block has a closed-form inverse, inside a geometric multigrid VV-cycle. A block-triangular pressure solve provides the electron-pressure response to transport and conduction and couples it to the field through the pressure gradient. The field block is solved approximately using multigrid-preconditioned inner GMRES within an outer flexible GMRES (FGMRES) solver.

To eliminate this cost, we follow [14] and employ an analytical mass matrix (AMM) approximation to the ion response in the Jacobian matrix. The resulting approximate Jacobian action employs no particle loop and only needs to store four values per node, and is thus extremely memory and cost friendly.

papers.title: MCUFlowNet: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Optical Flow on Microcontrollers
papers.abstract: Dense optical flow allows small drones to avoid obstacles. However, few dense optical flow networks are designed for microcontrollers (MCUs) with neural accelerators, whose on-chip SRAM limits the input resolution. We present PACE-NAS, a macro-to-micro neural architecture search framework that decouples memory from latency: a macro design fixes the backbone and its peak SRAM, and a micro design searches operators and depths to trade accuracy against compiler-estimated latency. We apply it to EdgeFlowNet on a Grove Vision AI V2 board (Ethos-U55), where profiling locates the peak SRAM at the full-resolution output head. Replacing transposed convolutions with bilinear upsampling and convolutions lowers the peak SRAM by 18%, and two lightweight context modules lower the endpoint error (EPE) without raising the peak. All searched subnets share this peak, so the search needs no memory constraint. We name the Pareto-optimal models MCUFlowNet; the fastest variant, MCUFlowNet-S, runs 1.76x faster than a retrained EdgeFlowNet at a 1.6% higher EPE and, in simulated forest flights at 2 m/s, reaches the goal without collision in 51.5% of trials, against 41.8%. PACE-NAS also applies to semantic segmentation, where a searched PIDNet-S variant runs 1.17x faster at similar accuracy. Code is available at https://gitlab.kuleuven.be/emedia-research-lab/esat-stadius/mcuflownet/mcuflownet.

papers.intro:
Small aerial robots rely on timely dense optical flow, the per-pixel displacement between consecutive frames, for collision avoidance [1], and on optical flow for autonomous landing and self-motion estimation [2]. Perception delay shortens the time available to avoid obstacles [3], which motivates onboard processing [4], and strict weight and power budgets favor microcontrollers (MCUs) [5].

Perception delay shortens the time available to avoid obstacles [3], which motivates onboard processing [4], and strict weight and power budgets favor microcontrollers (MCUs) [5].

EdgeFlowNet, a compact multi-scale network of standard convolutions, brings dense optical flow to the Coral Edge TPU [6], but on MCUs its full-resolution output head sets the peak SRAM and thus bounds the input resolution. Hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS) adapts networks to a target device [7]; on MCUs, it treats peak SRAM as a constraint and can be co-designed with the memory scheduling of the inference engine [8, 9]. For optical flow, however, NAS has typically targeted GPU-scale models [10], and few dense flow networks are designed for MCUs with neural accelerators.

This paper proposes PACE-NAS, a macro-to-micro framework for hardware-aware NAS that adapts existing dense flow networks to MCUs by decoupling memory from latency (Fig. 1). Its macro design profiles the target platform, restructures the layers that set the peak SRAM, and adds two lightweight context modules for image-wide context where SRAM is spare; these steps fix the backbone and its peak SRAM. Its micro design trains a weight-sharing supernet over operators and depths that leave this peak unchanged, then runs an evolutionary Pareto search over endpoint error (EPE) and the latency estimated by Arm’s Vela compiler [11]. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to use hardware-aware NAS to design dense optical flow networks for MCUs.

papers.title: Biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional sphere
papers.abstract: We prove that a proper biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional unit sphere $\mathbb S^4$ lies minimally in a small hypersphere of radius $1/\sqrt{2}$. Since the surfaces with constant mean curvature and those with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field are already understood, the core of the paper is the non-existence of biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in $\mathbb S^4$ whose mean curvature is not constant and whose normalized mean curvature vector field is not parallel. We first show, adapting an argument of Fu, Hong and Yang, that the gradient of the mean curvature is a principal direction. Then the problem reduces to a first order system of ordinary differential equations with a constraint, and we show that this system has no admissible solutions by an elimination argument.

papers.title: Splay ostracism on ferroelectric nematic shells
papers.abstract: Ostracism was the practice in use in Athens and other ancient Greek cities to send into exile citizens whose influence was deemed to be dangerous. Quite similarly, splay ostracism is here the approximation that bans splay distortion from thin films of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals on a curved shell in space. This reduces to a mere geometric problem the quest for equilibria of director vortexes and the walls isolating them, as splay ostracism requires the director field lines to be everywhere orthogonal to systems of geodesics on the shell. Consequences of this theorem are explored for shells with Gaussian curvature of either sign. The resulting quasi static dynamics reveals both cases where walls escape from the shell and cases where they are trapped on it, with possibly different reflections on the vortex dynamics.

Phenomenological theories have been proposed to describe the transition from the ordinary nematic phase to the ferroelectric one [7, 8], which however leave out the effects of depolarization that have so striking experimental manifestations [9]. These effects include domain formation and concentration of bound charges on interfaces. To account properly for them calls for a nonlocal variational theory. In Sect. II, we recall the existing theories and phrase them in a unifying formalism. There, we also introduce the notion of splay ostracism as a draconian approximation to treat depolarizing effects.

papers.title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Steel property models can perform well on random test splits even when they extrapolate poorly to unfamiliar alloys. SteelAgent couples metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with a language-model interface for property prediction, uncertainty reporting and inverse design. We examine how the choice of held-out unit changes the conclusions drawn from SteelBench tensile-strength evaluations. For gradient boosting, pooled out-of-fold $R^2$ fell from 0.859 on a random split to 0.113 when steel families were held out. Empirical coverage of nominal 90% prediction intervals ranged from 91.0% under random splitting to 37.6% on held-out sources. The effect of physics-derived features depended on the evaluation. They increased gradient-boosting $R^2$ by 0.2534 in a 17-family holdout analysis and decreased it by 0.358 in a separate four-grade laboratory analysis. We report group-level errors and a synthetic regression experiment illustrating how calibration can deteriorate on held-out groups. These results motivate reporting the evaluation population alongside a property estimate or compliance score.

papers.title: h-dichotomies via noncritical uniformity and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.

papers.intro:
The notion of an exponential dichotomy introduced by Perron [19] plays a central role in the qualitative theory of nonautonomous differential equations and dynamical systems. It expresses the existence of an invariant splitting into stable and unstable directions, with exponential contraction in forward time on the stable component and exponential contraction in backward time on the unstable component. The classical theory, originating in the work of Perron, has been developed extensively; see, for example, [2, 3, 4, 11, 20, 22]. For evolution families that are not invertible, the definition of a dichotomy requires particular care: backward evolution is available only on the unstable subspaces, on which the forward operators are required to induce isomorphisms.

papers.title: Stacking Stars: Minimum-Area Packing with and without Rotation
papers.abstract:
We study the problem of packing a given set of polygons into a minimum-area convex container, that is, placing them without overlap so as to minimize the area of their convex hull. Every previously known polynomial-time algorithm with a nontrivial approximation guarantee for packing polygons with arbitrary edge orientations required the polygons to be convex. In fact, an algorithm was not even known when every input polygon was a quadrilateral. We obtain such algorithms for the entire class of star-shaped polygons with unrestricted combinatorial complexity. The stars may be just translated or also rotated. In either case, we give an $O(\log n)$-approximation algorithm, where $n$ is the number of stars. Likewise, we get $O(\log n)$-approximation algorithms for bin and strip packing, assuming that the diameter of the stars is at most some (small) constant.
  Previous approximation algorithms for polygon packing focused on convex objects, and the analysis always relied on a density argument, i.e., if the area of the packed objects is at least a fraction $\rho$ of the area of the container, then we have a $(1/\rho)$-approximation. However, star-shaped polygons may need an arbitrarily large area to be packed, even when the total area of the stars approaches $0$ and each star has bounded diameter. This phenomenon prevents the use of density arguments.
  We instead establish a strong structural property about any packing: Even though the stars can fit together in complicated ways, we can reorganize them into simple stacks, replace these stacks by rectangles, and consider a packing of these rectangles. The rearrangement costs only a factor of $O(\log n)$, which stems from the number of size groups.
  We complement our algorithms by showing that both the translational and the rotational versions are APX-hard, even for constant complexity stars.

Packing problems are among the most fundamental and practically motivated problems in computational geometry and combinatorial optimization. They arise in a wide range of real-world scenarios, for instance when cutting shaped pieces from fabric, arranging parts for milling, waterjet cutting and laser cutting, and placing objects for 3D printing (see Figure 1). In many of these applications, the objects are irregular and nonconvex, and their edges are not restricted to a fixed set of orientations.

Packing problems are among the most fundamental and practically motivated problems in computational geometry and combinatorial optimization. They arise in a wide range of real-world scenarios, for instance when cutting shaped pieces from fabric, arranging parts for milling, waterjet cutting and laser cutting, and placing objects for 3D printing (see Figure 1). In many of these applications, the objects are irregular and nonconvex, and their edges are not restricted to a fixed set of orientations.

The bulk of the theoretical work on geometric packing has focused on axis-parallel rectangles; for surveys with hundreds of references, see [14, 39, 40, 15]. A smaller body of theoretical work considers packing convex polygons with unrestricted edge orientations. This includes algorithms for a constant number of pieces [8, 37, 5, 34] and approximation algorithms for arbitrary-sized input sets [6, 7, 2, 27, 1]. Related results concern geometric knapsack [29] and the exact complexity of packing under rotations [4]. For convex objects, classical techniques such as density arguments are effective.

Related results concern geometric knapsack [29] and the exact complexity of packing under rotations [4]. For convex objects, classical techniques such as density arguments are effective.

Packing nonconvex polygons remains poorly understood from the viewpoint of polynomial-time approximation algorithms. Early geometric methods capable of handling arbitrary simple polygons were developed by Milenkovic and by Daniels and Milenkovic [31, 32, 33, 30, 16]. They gave exact algorithms for several containment and enclosure problems, as well as algorithms allowing a controlled geometric error, but with running times exponential in the number of pieces. Further exact approaches to irregular nesting have been developed using constraint programming, mixed-integer programming, branch-and-bound and global optimization [13, 22, 9, 26]. Some of these methods solve a discretized version of the geometric problem, whereas methods addressing continuous placements generally apply only to relatively small instances. More recently, Gerlach, Hennies and Kleist [23] initiated the study of online packing of nonconvex orthogonal polygons.

The scarcity of polynomial-time worst-case results stands in sharp contrast to the extensive operations-research literature on irregular cutting and packing. A series of surveys and bibliographies collectively covering hundreds of works documents mathematical models, geometric techniques, exact approaches, heuristics and metaheuristics [19, 36, 18, 10, 11, 25, 28, 24]. Optimization-based approaches may certify optimality on manageable instances, sometimes only after discretizing the possible placements, whereas heuristic methods are designed to produce high-quality solutions in practice but typically provide no worst-case approximation guarantees. This research has led to multiple software systems used in practice.11 1 Examples of prominent commercial systems include SigmaNEST, Hypertherm ProNest, Lantek Expert, Autodesk Inventor Nesting, and MIRISYS. Representative open-source systems include Deepnest and SVGnest. The 2024 edition of the CG:SHOP Challenge (Computational Geometry: Solving Hard Optimization Problems) also concerned a packing problem involving irregular and nonconvex objects [21]. Thus, the theoretical gap does not reflect a lack of interest in irregular packing. Rather, there is a striking contrast between a mature experimental and operations-research literature and the very limited theory of polynomial-time approximation.

The scarcity of polynomial-time worst-case results stands in sharp contrast to the extensive operations-research literature on irregular cutting and packing. A series of surveys and bibliographies collectively covering hundreds of works documents mathematical models, geometric techniques, exact approaches, heuristics and metaheuristics [19, 36, 18, 10, 11, 25, 28, 24]. Optimization-based approaches may certify optimality on manageable instances, sometimes only after discretizing the possible placements, whereas heuristic methods are designed to produce high-quality solutions in practice but typically provide no worst-case approximation guarantees. papers.title: A Large-Sample Study of Interstellar Reddening in Galactic Star Clusters
papers.abstract: The interstellar reddening (extinction or absorption) is caused mainly by the dust grains of different sizes and compounds. All astrophysical observations are somehow affected by this effect, depending on the wavelength and location of the observed object. Different methods and techniques have been developed over the last nearly one hundred years to determine the reddening and to map the solar neighbourhood. The members of open clusters are a consistent population of stars formed together with a homogeneous metallicity. Therefore, the reddening can be estimated in a statistical way, avoiding all problems of single stars and spectral-energy-distribution fitting, for example. Other than for most available works, we can also use more massive upper main-sequence stars for the analysis. We used classical colour-colour diagrams (also known as the Q-method) for (B-V), (BP-RP), (U-B), (U-BP), (U-RP), and (U-G) to determine consistent mean reddening values and their errors. The corresponding standard lines for the fitting are independent of the age and metallicity. We determined colour excesses for 5377 Galactic open clusters covering Galactocentric distances from two to twenty kpc, respectively. The derived values were checked with existing dust and extinction maps. In general, we found good agreement. The solar neighbourhood of +-1500 pc shows a very patchy structure of the dust composition. Our results lay the foundations for constructing a new map of the reddening (dust) distribution and estimating clusters' metallicities by isochrone fitting, keeping the distances and reddening values fixed.

papers.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
papers.abstract: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it. We explore meta access---giving the assistant a structured, permissioned view of the interface itself and propose a ladder of levels: feature tutoring; metadata, settings, and preference access; retrieval over summaries and messages, confirmed mutation, and full orchestration. Meta access can turn a chat client from many screens into one entry point for finding, navigating, organising, and operating it, while raising risks around grounding, privacy, prompt injection, and trust. General-purpose agentic harnesses are runtimes; because they can change their own settings, meta access becomes reflexive and needs a separate control-plane boundary. We ground this in the Meta Chat prototype of the Chat AI client. It builds bounded context from, e.g., summaries, settings, and relevant messages; links references to conversations, topics, and personas; supports confirmed, reversible changes; offers a browsable tutorial library; and recommends personas as user-started conversations. By exposing application state in structured form, meta access can extend screen readers from widget descriptions to semantic workspace operations. Meta access thus turns chat from a window onto one conversation into a control layer for the whole workspace, extending chat toward agentic capability without surrendering user control. As assistants become embedded in IDEs, dashboards, office suites, and operating systems, AI-era interfaces should expose a structured, permissioned model of their state and capabilities, ideally by opening their existing metamodels through a debugger-like interface.

papers.title: The stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with harmonic potential in the full subcritical regime
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the complex Ginzburg-Landau dynamic associated with the harmonic oscillator, with a random force which is white in time and covers the full subcritical range in space. We are able to renormalise the non-linearity using the same constant as the one used to renormalise the problem associated to the Laplacian. By an extension of the problem to complex times, we are able to prove that the solution of the complex Ginzburg-Landau is equal in law to the solution of the purely dissipative case, i.e. the associated complex $\Phi^4$ model, but along a complex axis of time.

papers.title: The Zhukovskiy-Volterra gyroscope: geometry and reduction
papers.abstract: We describe a symplectic reduction of the Zhukovskiy integrable case of motion of a rigid body about a fixed point with a gyroscope in $\mathbb R^n$ to an integrable magnetic flow on a sphere $S^{n-1}$. We also present Zhukovskiy's geometric interpretation of motion of the Euler top with a gyroscope, aka the Zhukovskiy--Volterra gyroscope, and perform a symplectic reduction of this system to an integrable magnetic flow on a $2$-dimensional sphere.

papers.title: Quasi-polynomial-sized vertex multicut-mimicking networks and kernelization for Vertex Multiway Cut
papers.abstract:
We give deterministic polynomial-time constructions of vertex multicut-mimicking networks of quasi-polynomial size. Given a graph G, a terminal set T, and a positive integer c, our algorithm constructs a graph with |T|^7 c^{O( log c ) } vertices that preserves every minimum vertex multiway cut value of at most c, for every partition of the terminals. Setting c=|T| gives an exact vertex multicut-mimicking network with |T|^{O( log |T| ) } vertices, resolving an open question of Wahlstr\"om [ACM Transactions on Algorithms 2022], who showed a bound of \kappa^{O( log^3 \kappa)} for the edge multicut-mimicking variant, where \kappa:= \sum_{t \in T} |N_G(t)| is the capacity of the terminal set, which was later improved to \kappa^{O( log^2 \kappa)} by Anand, Lee, Li and Saranurak [STOC 2024].
  As applications of our vertex multicut-mimicking network, we obtain deterministic kernels of size k^{O( log k )} for Vertex Multiway Cut, p^{O(1)} k^{O(log k)} for Vertex Multicut with p requests and |\Gamma|^{O(1)} k^{O( log k)} for Group Feedback Vertex Set, where k is the deletion budget and \Gamma is a finite group. Our first kernelization result, in particular, resolves an open question by Wahlstr\"om [ACM Transactions on Algorithms 2022], which was reiterated in a recent survey on kernelization by Jansen [Computer Science Reviews 2026]. Also, to the best of our knowledge, our kernel for Vertex Multicut is the first one whose size is completely polynomial in p and (quasi-polynomial) super-polynomial only in k.
  Finally, again using our vertex multicut-mimicking network for graphs, we obtain a hyperedge multicut-mimicking network for hypergraphs, which preserves hypergraph edge-multicuts of size up to c, of size |T|^{O(1)} c^{O(log c)}. Our result removes the dependence on the rank of the hypergraph from the exponent of the size bound, that existed in prior work.

papers.title: An Information Bottleneck for Post-hoc Memorization Mitigation in LLMs
papers.abstract: Recent studies have shown that large language models (LLMs) can memorize and reproduce copyrighted training data, raising serious privacy and intellectual property concerns. In this work, we investigate whether memorization can be mitigated without modifying or retraining the underlying model through an information bottleneck. We propose a modular plug-and-play framework that inserts a nonparametric variational information bottleneck (NVIB) between a frozen LLM backbone and its language modeling head. By compressing the final hidden representations before token prediction, the proposed bottleneck aims to preserve general linguistic knowledge while filtering out highly specific memorized sequences. We evaluate our approach on memorization extraction tasks involving book passages and on standard language modeling benchmarks to measure the trade-off between memorization reduction and downstream utility. Our experiments show that the NVIB layer substantially reduces extractability while maintaining competitive performance on benchmark tasks. These results suggest that adding an information bottleneck offers a practical and architecture agnostic direction for post-hoc memorization mitigation in pretrained LLMs.

papers.title: On blow-up dynamics for the nonlinear wave equation and the harmonic map heat flow
papers.abstract:
This Ph.D. thesis concerns the blow-up analysis, and more precisely, the asymptotic decomposition into profiles of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. In Chapter 1, we present a unifying framework for finding profile decompositions in Hilbert spaces using the notion of dislocation spaces. The next chapters are then devoted to my publications.
  In the second chapter, we construct solutions to the focusing, energy-critical, nonlinear wave equation in dimension 4 and 5, exhibiting finite-time Type II blow-up precisely at the origin with a single profile and a prescribed polynomial blow-up rate of order $-1-
u$, where $
u > 1$ in 4D and $
u > 3$ in 5D. The major difference between dimension 4 and 5 consists in the renormalization procedure. In 4D, we essentially follow the Krieger-Schlag-Tataru scheme developed for the 3-dimensional equation, where the polynomial structure of the nonlinearity permits the use of simple algebraic manipulations to control error terms. By contrast, the 5D case requires a modified setup due to the lower regularity of the nonlinearity, which complicates the treatment of nonlinear error terms.
  In Chapter 3, we provide a modern presentation of classical Lp and Schauder estimates for parabolic equations. Then, in Chapter 4, we consider finite-time and $k$-equivariant solutions to the harmonic map heat flow from a disk to a sphere. Under general time-dependent, $k$-equivariant and smooth boundary data, we prove that the profile decomposition at the singular time contains only one bubble. The method relies on the maximum and comparison principle. We also prove a global existence criterion and exhibit solutions blowing up in infinite time for any degree of equivariance. Finally, the appendix presents the profile decomposition for the harmonic map heat flow proved by Struwe and Qing using energy arguments and the Palais-Smale condition.

papers.title: On the number of edges in quasiplanar graphs
papers.abstract: A $k$-quasiplanar graph is a graph drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges. Pach, Shahrokhi, and Szegedy conjectured that every such graph on $n$ vertices has $O_k(n)$ edges. ChatGPT produced a proof of this conjecture. Here, we present a simplified, self-contained version of that proof.

papers.title: $O(1/n)$ Convergence Rate for RVI $Q$-Learning
papers.abstract: We establish finite-time convergence guarantee for synchronous relative value iteration (RVI) $Q$-learning for finite weakly communicating Markov decision processes (MDPs). For stochastic Krasnosel'ski\u{\i}--Mann iterations driven by a non-expansive, linearly regular map on a finite-dimensional normed space, we establish last-iterate mean-squared residual bounds under martingale-difference noise whose conditional second moment grows at most linearly with the squared residual. Suitable polynomial stepsizes of order $n^{-a}$ yield an $O(n^{-a})$ rate for $0<a\leq1$. We verify linear regularity and the noise condition for the centered Bellman operator for finite weakly communicating MDPs. Applying the general result gives an $O(n^{-1})$ bound on the mean-squared Bellman span residual of RVI $Q$-learning iterates when a suitable stepsize sequence is used. The positive gap between optimal and suboptimal stationary deterministic policies then yields an $O(n^{-1})$ bound on the expected suboptimality of the greedy policy. Consequently, $O(\epsilon^{-1})$ synchronous iterations suffice for an $\epsilon$-optimal policy in expectation. These guarantees are instance-dependent, with constants that depend on the hitting-time parameters and the suboptimality gap of the second-best policy.

papers.title: Foresee to Trade: Forecast-Augmented Policy Optimization for Portfolio Management
papers.abstract: Online investment services must translate asset opportunities into investment outcomes for users' accounts, yet the same market opportunity can warrant different account actions. We study how supervision from future asset opportunities can strengthen account-level trading decisions and propose Forecast-Augmented Relative Policy Optimization (FRPO). FRPO separately supervises asset opportunities and account decisions through a jointly learned representation: a Financial State Head (FSH) learns future relative-return targets to provide asset-level opportunity supervision, while Same-Path Group-Relative Optimization compares trading trajectories under the same market path and initial account to provide account-level relative-outcome supervision. An Adaptive Gate coordinates auxiliary supervision using predictive variance and gradient alignment. FSH is used only during training; inference uses the encoder and policy for trading. Across DJIA30, TOPIX Core30, and three investment-style portfolios, ten-seed evaluations show that FRPO achieves the highest mean cumulative and annualized returns among the compared methods in all five settings. These results support strengthening investment agents' trading decisions through joint supervision from asset opportunities and trading outcomes.

papers.title: Thinking Is Not Writing: Designing AI Chatbots to Connect Reasoning and Revision
papers.abstract: Supporting students' argumentative writing with AI requires connecting reflection to their revision processes. We present Maike, a Socratic chatbot supporting writing through argument diagnosis, targeted questioning, and a student model across Think and Write modes. In a classroom study, 65 secondary-school students used Maike or a control chatbot sharing the interface, language model, and Think/Write modes. Approximately 40% of students improved their essay scores. However, Maike users engaged more in idea-level dialogue (56% vs. 44%) and moved iteratively between discussion and editing. Transitions from ideas discussed in dialogue to revisions were positively associated with score gains. These findings suggest a design target for AI writing support: coordinating reflection with revision. We contribute an architecture for supporting argumentative reasoning without generating essay text and an approach linking interaction patterns to writing processes and outcomes. As AI becomes embedded in classrooms, understanding these connections is essential to assessing (and designing for) its educational value.

papers.title: ZeroRAG: Adaptive Semantic Peer Routing for Decentralized Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a standard approach to enhance the reliability of large language model (LLM) outputs by retrieving documents relevant to a query and supplying them in the LLM prompt. Today's RAG systems collect, index, and serve these documents from centralized stores. In practice, however, documents are owned by organizations, devices, and individuals who cannot or will not surrender custody of them to a central party, e.g., because of privacy, copyright or regulatory compliance. Existing modern decentralized retrieval techniques either reintroduce a coordinating authority, or rely on a global data structure that requires continuous network-wide coordination (e.g., DHTs). We present ZeroRAG, a decentralized routing layer for document retrieval in RAG that performs semantic query routing across an overlay of peers with- out global data structures or centralized orchestration. Documents remain with the peers that own them, and each peer keeps only lightweight local state: a bounded set of neighbor advertisements and a cache of recently routed queries. Using these, ZeroRAG steers each query through a best-first walk that progressively rewires the overlay toward semantically relevant neighbors, so recall improves over time as the network self-organizes. We evaluate ZeroRAG using three real-world workloads and two decentralized baselines. We find that ZeroRAG outperforms baselines in terms of recall and required network messages, approaches the recall and LLM answer accuracy of a centralized document store, self-heals after catastrophic peer failures, and scales to 100 000 peers.

papers.title: On the Spectral Dependence of Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Tracking
papers.abstract:
We study how the spectral geometry of the mixing matrix enters the convergence of decentralized stochastic gradient tracking (GT) for smooth strongly convex problems. General bounds contain the factor $\Delta_\lambda^{-3}$ in the higher-order stochastic term, where $\Delta_\lambda$ is the absolute spectral gap. We show that, even for two agents with identical quadratic objectives, the exact steady-state mean-square disagreement scales as $\alpha^2\sigma^2\Delta_\lambda^{-3}$ as the nontrivial eigenvalue approaches $-1$, provided the stepsize $\alpha$ is sufficiently small relative to the gap. Here $\sigma^2$ is the gradient-noise variance. By unrolling the disagreement recursion, we establish a stochastic bound that averages all nontrivial eigenvalue contributions for diagonalizable mixing matrices, up to an eigenvector conditioning factor. As a real or complex eigenvalue approaches the unit circle away from $1$, its contribution grows as the inverse cube of its distance to the circle; growth can be slower near $1$. For symmetric mixing with gaps $p$ at $1$ and $
u$ at $-1$, the weighted sum $	heta_1/p+	heta_2/
u^3$ replaces the prior factor $(\Delta_\lambda
u^2)^{-1}$. For $N$ agents, $N	heta_1$ and $N	heta_2$ count the nonnegative and negative nontrivial eigenvalues, respectively. On a symmetric family, a finite-horizon lower bound for the average iterate matches the worst-case factor $p^{-1}+
u^{-3}$ up to universal constants. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted scaling.

papers.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
papers.abstract: We prove that K3 surfaces with no rational points over the finite field with $q$ elements exist if and only if $q \leq 11$. Our approach applies linear programming techniques to improve on generic sphere packing bounds for the discriminants of even rootless definite lattices. These bounds are applied to constrain the possible zeta functions of K3 surfaces with no rational points via the Artin--Tate formula. The remaining cases are ruled out by direct analysis of primitive embeddings of particular lattices into Niemeier lattices.

papers.title: Evaluating Language Model Features for Zero-Shot Time-Series Anomaly Detection Under Isolation Assumption
papers.abstract: Time-Series Anomaly Detection (TSAD) is a fundamentally challenging task: it is unsupervised, requires high local precision capabilities, and suffers from limited labelled data. Recent work has explored adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to time-series via cross-modal transfer. However, existing approaches are poorly suited to Multivariate TSAD (MTSAD), as tokenisation often obscures fine-grained temporal and variables structures, and most methods optimise auxiliary objectives such as forecasting or reconstruction. We posit that these surrogate objectives become unreliable as model capacity increases. Highly expressive models risk reconstructing or forecasting anomalies, undermining the foundations of both strategies. Instead, we propose to use LLMs purely as feature extractors and directly analyse their induced feature spaces. In this work, investigate the ability of LLMs to provide useful representations for MTSADs in a zero-shot setting through classification. To this end, we study the separability of the extracted features, under the assumption that anomalous features should be isolated from normal ones. We analyse their temporal and contextual discriminative ability using simple step-wise tokenisation schemes, with one time-step per token, which preserve fine-grained local information. Their usability for MTSAD is assessed using an unsupervised Isolation Forest, enabling a direct evaluation of the resulting representation quality. We further investigate whether the observed performance can be attributed to the language-related pre-training of the LLMs or arises independently of it. Our results provide empirical insight into the ability of LLMs to represent multivariate time-series for anomaly detection and highlight broader applications of cross-modal foundation models.

papers.title: A Projection-Coupled 2.5D THB-GIFT and Quadtree-SBIGA Formulation for Moving-Load Analysis in Semi-Infinite Media
papers.abstract: Moving loads in semi-infinite media generate extended wave fields while complex local structures require fine geometric and spatial resolution. This paper develops a projection-coupled two-and-a-half-dimensional (2.5D) THB-GIFT and quadtree-SBIGA computational formulation that assigns independent discretizations to these regions. The near-field THB-GIFT representation separates the geometry and analysis spaces and permits hierarchical local refinement, while the bounded propagation domain is discretized by quadtree-SBIGA with unified B\'ezier trace extraction and connected to the homogeneous unbounded exterior through a scaled-boundary impedance. On a common physical integration partition, an $L^2$ projection maps the nonmatching traces; Hermitian-adjoint force transfer then gives a virtual-work-consistent interface reduction. The regional dynamic operators and moving-load response reconstruction follow a single Fourier convention. Homogeneous half-space comparisons and a cylindrical-cavity analytical solution verify the components and the complete coupled system. In the cavity study, hierarchical THB refinement reduces the displacement error in the target inner band by a factor of approximately $41$. At a specified frequency--wavenumber point in the cavity benchmark, a comparison with matched outer-boundary discretization gives approximately $15\%$ lower sampled full-domain error for the coupled model, using $34\%$ fewer system degrees of freedom and $48\%$ fewer S-elements; the warm per-sample times are similar. A layered pavement with a buried conduit and twin modified-D tunnels demonstrate open, closed and multiple disconnected nonmatching interfaces and the analysis of local structural demand and dynamic interaction under moving loads.

papers.title: A Low Similarity Score Does Not Show Independence after Source-Conditioned Repository Rewriting
papers.abstract: Maintainers sometimes cite a low token-similarity score as evidence that an LLM-assisted rewrite of a copyleft project is independent of the original. We test what such a score can support under \emph{source-conditioned} rewriting: a coding agent keeps the original in its working copy, rewrites the repository, and iterates until a fixed behavioural harness passes, with no human edit to the code. On 69 rewrites of six copyleft Python projects we find that: \ding{182}~Agent-only rewriting is inexpensive and often yields low scores. Every controlled rewrite passes the harness after repair, usually within half an hour for the initial rewrite. Under a ground-up rearchitecture prompt, most rewrites fall below 25\% JPlag similarity and still pass the harness. \ding{183}~A single low score is an unreliable witness. Identical project--agent--prompt configurations produce wide spreads in similarity; run-to-run variation dominates project and agent effects, and in more than a third of configurations the three repeats straddle the threshold. Rewrites retain more of the original's imports and fingerprint facts than unrelated projects do, yet hand-written independent implementations of the same task often retain as much, and neither signal separates the two groups better than chance. Thus a low score on one rewrite is weak evidence of independence: another run of the same agent may score high. Claims based on similarity should report repeated generations, and candidate provenance signals should be checked against same task independent implementations, not only against unrelated projects.

papers.title: Rotation Is Token-Blind: A Structural Criterion for Post-Training Quantization of Feed-Forward Geometry Transformers
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D models use Transformers to predict camera poses, depth, and structure in one pass, avoiding iterative multi-view optimization. Long sequences and deep attention incur high compute and memory costs, motivating Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) for deployment. Existing PTQ methods mainly suppress channel-wise outliers by smoothing or orthogonal rotation. Geometry Transformers introduce a different challenge: heterogeneous token types share one activation quantization grid. A few special tokens may exert high leverage over global outputs and be updated by only a subset of blocks. Token-blind transforms, which apply the same transformation to every token, reduce overall quantization error but cannot remove differentiated degradation across token types. We propose QMapAnything, a structure-aware PTQ framework. We cast floating-point-preserving rotation and smoothing as a token-blind reparameterization group, and prove that they yield common-mode gains while leaving relative token SNR unchanged. We introduce a statistic $\Gamma$ that combines a special token's quantization disadvantage and output leverage to predict whether differentiated bias correction is needed beyond rotation. Experiments on geometric benchmarks show that W4A8 closely matches full-precision performance. Under W8A8, peak memory falls by $2.2$--$3.1\times$ versus FP32, with up to $3.1\times$ speedup on real hardware. These results provide a principled and efficient approach to deploying feed-forward 3D reconstruction models in resource-constrained edges.

papers.title: High precision timing of seven binary millisecond pulsars with the European Pulsar Timing Array
papers.abstract: Binary millisecond pulsars (MSPs) serve as exceptional astrophysical laboratories for a wide range of astrophysical studies, all of which rely on precise property measurements allowed by pulsar timing. In this paper, we present high-precision timing solutions for seven binary MSPs monitored by the European Pulsar Timing Array. By combining data collected from the five largest radio telescopes in Europe, as well as their coherently combined form, the Large European Array for Pulsars, we achieve phase-coherent timing solutions for all seven pulsars. We conduct a Bayesian timing and noise analysis on the combined data, yielding measurements of astrometric and orbital parameters with broadly improved precision, some reported for the first time. For PSRs J0125-2327, J1741+1351 and J2043+1711, we determine their distances and transverse velocities from astrometric measurements, and infer their masses via Shapiro delay measurements. Additionally, we examine the various contributions to the secular orbital-period variations for PSRs J0125-2327, J1125+7819 and J1741+1351, and estimate their kinematic distances. For PSRs J0125-2327 and J1741+1351, we detect the signature of annual-orbital parallax in the timing data. This allows us to derive a strongly favored, unique solution for the orbital ascending node and inclination angle for PSR J0125-2327, and a tightly constrained ascending node for PSR J1741+1351. Moreover, we use the orbital periods and their derivatives for several binary MSPs to place upper limits on gravitational-wave strain in both the sub-nanohertz and microhertz frequency regimes. Our results show that the orbits of binary MSPs could provide stringent constraints in microhertz range, thereby possibly complementing standard pulsar-timing-array analyses in the future.

papers.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
papers.abstract: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs. For individual DMs, the correlation with the bandpowers is at the per cent level. Neglecting the cross-covariance changes the width of the $\chi^2$ distribution by only 0.8 per cent, so the two observables can be treated as effectively independent for wide-area surveys. In a joint forecast with an LSST-like weak lensing survey, adding the Macquart relation tightens constraints on the physical baryon density by 32 per cent and on the mean host contribution by a factor of 4.1, while improving baryonification parameters by only about 5 per cent, indirectly through the host contribution. Finally, we show that the redshift distribution of FRBs without identified hosts, which enters every DM power spectrum, can be reconstructed by inverting their DMs with the jointly fitted mean relation without biasing the inferred parameters, whereas a 20 per cent error in the mean relation biases the DM power spectrum by up to 2$\sigma$ per band for $5\times 10^5$ FRBs.

papers.title: Adapting Qwen3 to Tajik from 0.6B to 8B: Lower Text Loss Did Not Mean Better Understanding
papers.abstract: Small LoRA adapters trained on Tajik news and books lowered Qwen3's Tajik text loss at every size we tried, from 0.6B to 8B, by 0.60 to 1.45 nats per token, but none of them improved Tajik reading comprehension where it can be measured. On Belebele the 1.7B and 8B adapters left accuracy unchanged and the 4B adapter lowered it by 3.7 points; at 0.6B the score rose by 4.2 points but sits near chance and coincides with a change in which answer letter the model prefers, so we do not read it as understanding. At 8B, continued pretraining on about 375 million tokens of raw Tajik text was followed by a Belebele gain of 9.9 points. After a further supervised fine-tuning stage, our main model, e3, is 11.4 points above Qwen3-8B on Belebele; its English MMLU changed by -1.2 points, and a loss larger than 3.3 points is excluded. The same heavy recipe applied to Qwen3-0.6B-Base brought its text loss close to that of the 8B model after books-only pretraining, while its multiple-choice answers stayed near chance and its English MMLU fell by 7.6 points. We report 15 trained models and their 5 starting models from June to October 2025, scored in 2026 on one harness with paired intervals, and we report what went wrong: lost training records, a thinking-mode dataset with almost no reasoning in it, later branches whose training data was never documented, and a 4-bit release that contains no transformer layers.

papers.title: BrainPFN: Amortized Brain-Behaviour Prediction via Prior-Data Fitted Networks
papers.abstract: The standard approach to predicting behavioral phenotypes from functional MRI is represented by Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR) applied on functional connectivity (FC) matrices. However, this approach is limited: separate models must be fit and tuned for every score and cohort, they do not transfer across datasets, and accuracy degrades sharply when only a handful of subjects are available, as is typical of clinical or cognitive studies. Despite an increasing interest in developing brain foundation models, none has consistently outperformed KRR on behaviour prediction; most reported gains come from easier targets such as age, sex, or diagnosis rather than continuous behavioural scores. We introduce BrainPFN, a Prior Data Fitted Network for brain behaviour regression. BrainPFN is meta-trained on a domain-specific prior built from ~7k real FC matrices, from which we sample one billion synthetic training samples. At inference, a labelled context is simply passed through the network in a single forward pass, with no per-score or per-cohort refitting required. Across four independent cohorts, BrainPFN beats KRR on small sample prediction, and leads recent foundation models pre-trained at four to nine times larger scale. Our meta-training pool, aggregated from open repositories, is a fraction of the size of the corpora behind competing models, most of which sit behind restrictive data use agreements such as UK Biobank. We release this pool publicly alongside code and checkpoints, showing that a modest, openly available pool can match or beat models trained at Biobank scale.

papers.title: Canonical Correlation Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Relational inductive biases such as grids or graphs allow neural networks with fewer trainable parameters and improved generalization, but require a known structure beforehand. When no structure is available, the covariance matrix provides a principled substitute, and coVariance Neural Networks (VNNs) have shown that using it yields models that are theoretically grounded in Principal Component Analysis, stable to finite-sample estimation errors and parameter-efficient. This framework, however, is limited to single-view data, whereas many applications observe the same phenomenon through multiple views, each with its own in-view covariance and a cross-view covariance linking them. To incorporate these matrices as inductive biases in a principled way, we introduce CAnonical correlation NEural networks (CANEs), architectures that use in-view and cross-view covariances as distinct relational biases to solve downstream tasks. Via spectral analysis, CANEs draw analogies with Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA), a classical technique to project two-view data onto a correlated subspace. However, while CCA's objective is to compute shared view representations, CANEs are trained to solve a downstream task directly. We bound their output error under finite-sample covariance perturbations and show that it depends on controllable Lipschitz constants of the learned filters in place of the singular-value gap that governs the stability of CCA, thus guaranteeing better robustness. Experiments on seven datasets from brain imaging and motion sensing show that CANEs match or outperform single-view, two-view and CCA-based baselines, often with fewer parameters, and retain their performance when covariances are re-estimated from fewer samples.

papers.title: Copula-Based Dependence Modeling for Resilient 6G Multi-Hop Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Reliable operation of multi-hop wireless networks requires accounting for statistical dependence among link failures caused by common propagation conditions and shared network components. This paper develops a copula-based framework for modeling node-induced dependence among link-level signal-to-noise ratios and quantifying its effect on end-to-end outage. By separating marginal fading distributions from the dependence structure, the framework captures nonlinear and tail-dependent coupling beyond conventional correlation-based models. Exact outage expressions are derived for primary-backup configurations involving edge-disjoint paths and paths with shared links. We then characterize the conditional outage probability of each candidate backup path given a primary-path failure, jointly accounting for node-induced dependence and shared-link failures. In high-reliability regimes, we derive a first-order score that decomposes conditional outage into terms associated with marginal path outage, shared links, and node-induced dependence, enabling efficient dependence-aware backup-path selection. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the first-order and exact selection rules identify the same backup path. Numerical results validate the analysis and show that copula families with the same Kendall's $\tau$ can yield markedly different outage behavior because of their different tail-dependence properties. In particular, lower-tail dependence and path overlap can substantially reduce redundancy gains and reverse rankings based only on marginal outage probability.

papers.title: Multiplicity via symmetry for the Minkowski mean curvature equation: Dirichlet and Neumann problems
papers.abstract: We consider the Minkowski mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =\lambda u+\mu h(x,u) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \quad \mathcal B u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial \Omega, $$ where $\mathcal B \in \{ \mathcal D, \mathcal N \}$ is a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition and $\Omega$ is a smooth bounded domain, required to be convex in the Neumann case. Moreover, $\lambda, \mu \geq0$ are parameters, and $h(x,u)$ is odd with respect to $u$ and positive for $u > 0$. Using minmax methods in nonsmooth critical point theory, we prove that $\lambda>\lambda^\mathcal B_k$ yields at least $k$ pairs of nontrivial solutions with negative energy for every $\mu\geq0$, where $\lambda_k^\mathcal B$ are the corresponding Laplacian eigenvalues, indexed by $\lambda^\mathcal B_0=0$. Moreover, if $H(x,u):=\int_0^u h(x,t)\,dt=o(u^2)$ as $u\to0$, we prove that for $\lambda\in[\lambda^\mathcal B_k,\lambda^\mathcal B_{k+1})$ and every $j\geq\max\{1,k\}$, sufficiently large $\mu$ yields at least $2j-k$ distinct pairs of solutions: $j$ with negative energy and $j-k$ with positive energy.

papers.title: Estimating Vertical Ocean Velocity from Horizontal Currents: Linear and Depth-Conditional Neural-Network Approaches on a High-Resolution Regional Ocean Model
papers.abstract: The vertical component of the ocean velocity, w, is several orders of magnitude smaller than the horizontal components u and v, yet it controls vertical tracer transport, upwelling, and mixed-layer ventilation. Because w is extremely difficult to measure directly and is normally obtained only diagnostically from the continuity equation, predicting it from the horizontal velocity field is a problem of both practical and physical interest. We address this problem with two data-driven methods, a physically-motivated linear baseline and a convolutional neural network conditioned on depth through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM). Both methods are applied to a high-resolution regional simulation of the Coastal and Regional Ocean Community model over the Western Mediterranean, using a sub-region of the south-west Mediterranean Sea as a training region and two independent, out-of-sample regions for validation: the Alboran Sea, with a distinct dynamical regime driven by Atlantic inflow through the Strait of Gibraltar, and a transition region between Almer\'ia and Cartagena, between the Alboran Sea and the open western Mediterranean. Once the FiLM network is regularized enough to avoid overfitting to a single training domain, we find that its comparison with the physically interpretable linear baseline is domain- and depth-dependent rather than uniform: near the reference depth, essentially all of the achievable out-of-sample performance on both validation domains is already captured by the linear model, but at the deepest levels tested the FiLM network outperforms the linear baseline on the transition domain, whereas on Alboran it does not.

papers.title: A Wigner-Lindblad phase space model for open quantum dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate the collisional quantum dynamics of an open system in contact with a thermal bath. We propose a particle-bath interaction model based on the Weyl quantization principle and the Wigner phase space description of quantum evolution. By factorizing the reduced Hamiltonian of the open system via supersymmetric quantum mechanics techniques, we construct system-dependent creation and annihilation operators for arbitrary potential landscapes. This allows us to extend the classical Fokker--Planck relaxation mechanism to incorporate Lindblad quantum stochastic jumps within the Wigner phase-space formalism. Through a semiclassical expansion of the Moyal star product to second order, we obtain a generalized Wigner--Lindblad kinetic model featuring position-dependent friction and diffusion terms. We establish the mathematical well-posedness of the Lindblad problem and we validate our approach through numerical simulations. Our model resolves unphysical long-time artifacts of standard quantum Fokker--Planck models in quartic double-well traps, accurately captures dissipative quantum state localization in 2D molecular potentials (4D phase space), and effectively evaluates electron transport and trapping times in InAs/InP resonant tunneling diodes.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global H\"older regularity
papers.abstract:
Let $ C_\omega$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $\omega\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_\omega$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $\beta^+>0>\beta^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $\beta^\pm$.
  As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/\beta^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-\Delta_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_\omega$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$.
  The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global H\"older regularity for $(-\Delta_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible H\"older exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.

papers.title: Extensions to the Dubins Airplane Method - Flight Performance Constraints in Uniform Wind
papers.abstract: This paper extends the Dubins Airplane Method to generate trajectories for fixed-wing aircraft that remain within flight performance limits in the presence of uniform wind. Within the field of runtime-efficient trajectory generation for fixed-wing aircraft, the Dubins Airplane Method represents a well-received and widely adopted compromise between algorithmic complexity, runtime efficiency, and solution quality. However, its simplistic kinematic model restricts its ability to generate safe and feasible trajectories, especially in the presence of wind. As a mathematical foundation to overcome these limitations, a set of closed-form equations are derived that relate flight performance constraints to kinematic constraints. Building upon existing methods that use trochoids for planning of 2D trajectories in uniform wind, this paper presents a set of iterative algorithms for planning versatile 3D trajectories composed of trochoidal or circular turns and straight flight segments, with constant vertical speed, constant thrust or smooth longitudinal transitions. The presented methods comprise a flexible and modular framework for runtime-efficient generation of performance-aware trajectories based on parametric curves without the need for numerical trajectory representations.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Reinforcement Learning for Keypoint Positioning of Deformable Linear Objects
papers.abstract: Deformable linear object (DLO) manipulation is challenging because high-dimensional configurations, nonlinear contact dynamics, and diverse material and geometric properties produce a broad range of object responses that are both difficult to model and data-intensive to learn. This work studies reinforcement learning for planar manipulation of a one-end-grasped DLO, focusing on training efficiency, observation design, robustness, and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. We compare three Proximal Policy Optimization training stacks and find that the GPU-parallel MuJoCo Playground stack enables faster convergence and more consistent performance than CPU-based alternatives under the same wall-clock budget. Relative keypoint observations and an asymmetric actor-critic formulation further improve learning efficiency. Policies trained with observation noise, delay, domain randomization, and disturbances achieve simulation success rates of 96.4% for single-point tracking, 98.0% for disturbance recovery, and 88.8% for two-point tracking. Using markerless RGB-D keypoint estimation, the policies transfer without real-world fine-tuning, succeeding in 9/10, 10/10, and 8/10 physical trials, respectively.

papers.title: Flexible Piezoelectric Tactile Sensing System for Intelligent Object Recognition
papers.abstract: Tactile sensing provides information about object properties that can improve robotic grasping and manipulation. However, accurate object recognition during the early stages of grasping remains challenging, particularly under strict real-time constraints. This study presents a flexible, distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing system for early-stage object recognition. The system was experimentally evaluated using six everyday objects and three recognition approaches: feature-based classification using support vector machines (SVMs), raw-signal classification using 1D convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs) and convolutional recurrent neural networks (C-RNNs), and spatiotemporal heatmap classification using a 2D-CNN. The effects of sensor count and temporal window size on recognition accuracy and real-time feasibility were systematically investigated. Increasing the number of sensing elements improved recognition performance across all approaches. The best-performing method, based on spatiotemporal heatmaps and a 2D-CNN, achieved F1-scores of 0.9796, 0.9846, and 0.9903 using 16, 24, and 32 sensors, respectively. The optimal configuration, comprising 32 sensors and a 100-ms temporal window (50 samples), was deployed on an embedded edge platform, achieving an end-to-end recognition latency of approximately 101 ms from contact onset and an energy consumption of 63.8 microjoules per inference. These results demonstrate the potential of distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing for accurate, energy-efficient, and real-time object recognition during robotic grasping.

papers.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions
papers.abstract:
Type theories designed for mathematics or program verification need only that a proposition holds; proof irrelevance in conversion erases, at the kernel level, how a claim was established. A persistent knowledge store, by contrast, must retain that record: who established a claim, by which derivation or external tool, and under which assumptions. This volume presents the theory of Eigenius---a store of typed knowledge over constructive institutions---and develops its metatheory from that requirement.
  The kernel theory is a dependent type theory with cumulative universes, an impredicative universe of propositions, inductive families, and an intensional identity type. Proof irrelevance is an axiom with an explicit witness rather than a conversion rule, so proofs of a proposition are provably equal yet remain distinct terms. Definitional equality is joinability under an orthogonal rewriting system---confluent, injective on type formers, and decidable by a type-free test---while a separate subsumption judgment covers universe cumulativity, codomain-covariant function types, and declared class inclusions.
  We prove consistency via a set-theoretic model; develop a justification logic over the kernel's propositions to track evidence and support; organize environments as an institution so that store extensions are signature morphisms and external verdicts enter via comorphisms; formulate a typed knowledge-graph theory with records, classes, and refinements; and prove the correctness of conversion, normalization by evaluation, and bidirectional type checking relative to termination. A Lean 4 formalization accompanies the volume.

papers.title: Curvature by Design: A Support Structure for Continuum Robots
papers.abstract: Constant- and piecewise-constant-curvature models are widely used to simplify the kinematics of continuum robots, although the assumed curvature profiles are not necessarily inherent mechanical properties of the robot and may therefore be violated during operation. Rather than assuming a prescribed curvature profile in the kinematic model and estimating deviations from it, this paper presents a multi-segment scissor-based support structure that mechanically constrains a continuum robot to exhibit prescribed constant or spatially varying curvature profiles. The design uses Taylor approximations to enable an overconstrained multi-joint linkage to predictably distribute global bending among the small-angle movements of multiple flexures. The geometric coupling is realized using compliant flexure joints, enabling the support structure to be manufactured as a single piece. The structure is integrated with a tendon-actuated continuum robot with a flexible backbone. Experiments show that the structure makes the robot resistant to deformations other than the prescribed curvature, significantly enhancing shape precision compared to classical flexible-backbone designs. This constrains the robot from making S-shapes when external loads are applied in the opposite direction of the bending. By mechanically constraining the admissible deformation, the proposed structure reduces the number of independent shape variables that must be estimated.

papers.title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
papers.abstract:
Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action.
  We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(E\Phi^2+P(\Phi))}d\Phi$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $d\Phi$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(\Phi)=\frac{\lambda}{4}\Phi^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.

papers.title: The infrared unmodulated pyramid wavefront sensor: simulations, lab and on sky
papers.abstract: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets requires strong suppression of stellar light at small angular separations, achievable with extreme adaptive optics (XAO). The pyramid wavefront sensor (PWFS) is widely used for its sensitivity but suffers from nonlinearities and limited dynamic range. Modulation extends the range but reduces sensitivity and limits loop speed. We investigate an unmodulated infrared PWFS (IR-umPWFS), where the dynamic range scales with wavelength, removing the need for modulation and enabling faster operation. We adopt a 3-sided PWFS, which eliminates the roof defect of the classical 4-sided design. We assess its feasibility and performance through end-to-end simulations, lab tests, and on-sky observations on the PAPYRUS bench at the Observatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP), and compare it with a visible modulated PWFS (VIS-mPWFS). Simulations show reliable operation, reaching Strehl ratios up to ~60% at 1400 nm for seeing up to 4''. Infrared operation improves linearity, reduces optical-gain variations and modal cross-talk. Laboratory results validate the simulations and confirm the pyramid quality. On sky, stable closed-loop operation was achieved over three nights. Compared with the VIS-mPWFS at 500 Hz, the IR-umPWFS at 1000 Hz showed gains of ~1.63 in Strehl ratio and ~1.26 in encircled energy, and a ~2.03-fold reduction in residual wavefront error. The IR-umPWFS remained robust to tip-tilt offsets up to 3 lambda/D at 1400 nm. It is a strong candidate for future XAO systems: operating in the infrared extends the linear range sufficiently to remove the need for modulation, enabling higher loop speeds no longer limited by the modulation mirror, which contributed to the improved on-sky performance. The OHP turbulence (D/r0 ~ 17 at 1400 nm) is comparable to typical VLT conditions (D/r0 ~ 20), supporting the relevance of these results for VLT/RISTRETTO.
