papers.title: Strict unimodality without log-concavity for partial Petrial polynomials
papers.abstract: For a simple graph $G$, the partial Petrial polynomial $P_G^{\times}(z)$ enumerates all diagonal perturbations of its adjacency matrix over $GF(2)$ by rank. We derive a rooted attachment identity and apply it to the tree $R_m$ obtained by joining a new vertex to the middle vertex of each of $m$ disjoint copies of the five-vertex path. We prove that the nonzero coefficient sequence of $P_{R_m}^{\times}(z)$ is strictly unimodal for every $m\ge1$, but is log-concave if and only if $1\le m\le3$. Thus the $21$-vertex tree $R_4$ provides an explicit strictly unimodal, non-log-concave example. For $m\ge5$, the unique mode occurs at degree $\lfloor(149m+85)/32\rfloor$. More generally, for any fixed path rooted at an internal vertex, joining a new vertex to the roots of sufficiently many disjoint copies produces a tree whose partial Petrial polynomial is not log-concave.

papers.title: Understanding Data Influence in Transportation Networks: A Physics-Constrained Influence-Function Framework
papers.abstract: Understanding how individual training observations influence model predictions is important for developing reliable and interpretable data-driven transportation systems. Existing influence-function methods, however, are primarily formulated for unconstrained learning and do not explicitly account for physical constraints that couple different components of a transportation network. Under such constraints, perturbing a training observation can affect model parameters and predictions only through physically feasible directions, potentially changing how its influence propagates across the network. This paper develops a hard physics-informed influence-function framework for constrained learning, in which training-data influence is characterized within the physically feasible space defined by network constraints. The analytical results reveal how physical constraints alter the magnitude, direction, and spatial distribution of training-sample influence relative to conventional influence measures. Using traffic prediction under flow-conservation constraints as a case study, we show that influential observations identified by the proposed framework differ systematically from those identified by classical influence functions. Through orthogonal decomposition, we quantitatively characterize how much of a perturbation in the training data is propagated through the network via the flow-conservation constraints and how much is removed by the constraint projection. The proposed influence framework provides a physically consistent approach for evaluating training-data influence in constrained transportation learning problems, with potential applications to data diagnostics, sensor evaluation, and targeted data collection.

papers.title: MV-Sign: Multi-View 3D Motion Integration and Enhanced Text-to-Motion Conditioning for Sign Language Production
papers.abstract: Sign language production (SLP) aims to generate appropriate sign language motion from spoken language text. However, current 3D SLP methods suffer from noisy supervision and weak text conditioning. Specifically, these methods typically rely on pseudo-3D motion data fitted from single-view frontal videos, which introduces severe self-occlusion and loses fine-grained hand details, ultimately degrading downstream production. To overcome these limitations, we propose a comprehensive framework that jointly integrates multi-view 3D motion data and optimizes the text-conditioning pathway. First, we introduce How2Sign-MV3D, a high-fidelity dataset constructed via a novel cross-view curation pipeline that fuses multi-view estimates to resolve occlusions and filter non-signing segments. Second, we design a robust SLP model incorporating a sign-aware spatio-temporal VQ-VAE (ST-VQVAE) for joint body-hand tokenization, a pseudo-gloss adapter, and keyframe-aware retrieval to enhance text-to-motion alignment. Evaluated on the How2Sign benchmark, our framework reduces body and hand DTW-PA-JPE by 32.8% and 20.9% respectively compared to the state-of-the-art. Finally, we release two new high-quality 3D datasets, ASLCitizen-3D and MM-WAuslan-MV3D, alongside SGNify-MV as a multi-view video benchmark to support broader community research.

papers.title: Optimal Competitive Ratios for Chasing Convex Functions with Quadratic Growth
papers.abstract:
Chasing convex function has attracted much attention in recent years, which can be formulated as a game between a learner and an adversary. In each round, the adversary reveals a convex function, and the learner selects a decision and incurs a hitting cost and a movement cost for changing its decision. The performance of the learner is measured by the \emph{competitive ratio}, which compares its cumulative cost with that of an optimal offline decision sequence. For Euclidean movement, existing upper and lower bounds for $\kappa$-well-conditioned functions exhibit a polynomial gap. For squared Euclidean movement, dimension-free competitive guarantees have been established under quadratic growth, but the optimal competitive ratio remains unclear.
  In this paper, we establish optimal dimension-free competitive ratios for convex function chasing under two types of movement costs. For Euclidean movement, we propose Clipped Proximal Descent (CPD), which combines a balanced proximal step with a clipped correction toward the current minimizer. CPD achieves an $O(\kappa^{1/3})$ competitive ratio for smooth convex functions satisfying quadratic growth, improving the previous $O(\sqrt{\kappa})$ upper bound and matching the existing $\Omega(\kappa^{1/3})$ lower bound. For squared Euclidean movement, we establish the exact optimal dimension-free competitive ratio for convex functions satisfying quadratic growth. Our result is based on a new tight competitive analysis of Regularized Online Balanced Descent (R-OBD) and a matching lower bound against randomized algorithms.

papers.title: Minimal surfaces with density two at infinity
papers.abstract: We prove that a connected, properly embedded minimal surface without boundary in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and with density two at infinity is a catenoid or a singly periodic Scherk surface.

papers.title: STAG-Net: Structure-Aware Attention over Landmark Groups for Lightweight Head Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Head pose estimation is important for human computer interaction and driver monitoring, but many image based methods remain too costly for resource constrained deployment. We propose STAG-Net, a structure-aware attention over landmark groups for lightweight head Pose estimation that estimates head pose from facial landmarks using movement aware selection, spatial clustering, compact DeepSet encoders, self attention, and a global geometry descriptor. We develop variants using FaceMesh and Face Alignment Network landmarks and evaluate them under cross dataset and subject independent protocols on 300W-LP, AFLW2000, and BIWI. STAG-Net achieves the lowest mean absolute error among all compared landmark based methods in every evaluated setting. On BIWI frames with valid detections, the FAN variant also records the lowest overall error among all compared methods, reaching $3.51^\circ$ under cross dataset evaluation and $2.39^\circ$ under subject independent evaluation. The regressors use only 0.012 to 0.043 million parameters and 24.1 to 83.6 thousand FLOPs, about three orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs than FSA-Net. Despite including landmark extraction and regression, the FaceMesh pipeline reaches 322.9 frames per second on a Tesla T4 GPU, nearly twice the 164.5 frames per second of the fastest measured image based baseline, and 111.0 frames per second on CPU. After normalization by dataset size, STAG-Net processes training samples seven to eight times faster than FSA-Net and more than one hundred times faster than HopeNet and TokenHPE, while complete training finishes within 28 minutes. These results show that STAG-Net combines leading landmark based accuracy with substantially lower training and inference cost.

papers.title: NUMA-Torch: Compiler-Driven NUMA-Aware LLM Prefill on Multi-Socket CPUs
papers.abstract: For sufficiently large transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs), whose parameters cannot be retained in on-chip caches, prefill throughput on multi-socket CPUs is often limited by sustainable DRAM bandwidth rather than peak floating-point throughput. In the standard PyTorch compilation (i.e., TorchInductor) path, model weights are allocated without considering the Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology: specifically, the affinity between memory banks and compute cores is disregarded. This causes a substantial fraction of weight accesses to traverse the inter-socket interconnect, severely degrading the effective memory bandwidth available to each socket. We address this bottleneck through a compiler-level solution that makes TorchInductor NUMA-aware. Treating each NUMA socket as an independent tensor-parallel partition, we introduce NUMA-aware Tensor Parallelism (NUMA-TP). This approach transparently shards weights across sockets and schedules compute kernels such that thread pools and memory allocations remain strictly local to their respective sockets using CPU affinity. We evaluate the approach on GPT-2 (117M, 345M, 762M) and BERT (Small, Large), which exercise standard multi-head attention and MLP, as well as Gemma 3 270M, which combines Multi-Query Attention with a GeGLU-gated MLP. By strictly enforcing data locality, our approach successfully mitigates cross-socket traffic, achieving prefill speedups of up to 2.63x on a dual-socket Haswell platform, up to 1.87x on a dual-socket Cascade Lake platform, and up to 2.27x on a four-socket Haswell-EX platform.

Driven by the necessity of accommodating many cores, modern high-performance servers have universally adopted Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) architectures [4]. There is consequently a tremendous, yet underutilized, potential to deploy Large Language Model (LLM) inference on these multi-socket CPU platforms, given their cost-effectiveness, broad availability, and the frequent absence of GPUs in deployment environments. The prefill phase of LLM inference which processes the full input prompt in one forward pass is traditionally assumed compute-bound owing to the high arithmetic intensity of dense matrix multiplications over long sequences. Yet on multi-socket CPUs under the standard TorchInductor compilation pipeline, prefill unexpectedly becomes severely DRAM-bound as NUMA-oblivious memory allocations force massive cross-socket traffic.

As illustrated in Figure 1, we view each socket of a multi-socket NUMA CPU as an independent node owning its locally attached DRAM and memory controller, together with cores that have private L1/L2 caches and share an L3. Sockets are linked by a QPI/UPI interconnect serving as the inter-rank network; accesses to another socket’s memory must cross it, incurring substantially higher latency and lower bandwidth than local accesses, and are therefore treated as explicit communication in our compilation model.

In standard execution, compute threads are distributed across all cores without regard to data locality, causing roughly half of all weight accesses to incur remote DRAM latency and saturating the inter-socket link. To empirically validate this, we conducted a Roofline analysis using Intel Advisor [5] on the kernels that dominate the prefill phase of a GPT-2 345M model [1] (batch size 1, sequence length 4096) on a dual-socket Haswell platform (Figure 2). For TorchInductor-compiled unmodified Triton-CPU baseline (circles), these kernels exhibit poor data locality and sit near the main-DRAM bandwidth ceiling, confirming that the prefill operates firmly in the DRAM-bound regime. Our NUMA-Torch path (triangles) improves core-to-memory affinity and, as the trajectory arrows indicate, shifts the kernels toward the higher-bandwidth L3 and L2 cache tiers, increasing overall throughput (GFLOPS).

Despite this architectural reality, existing CPU optimization efforts frequently overlook the NUMA penalty, focusing on intra-core compute optimizations. Addressing this NUMA-induced DRAM bandwidth wall must instead be the primary objective, and the most direct solution is strict enforcement of data locality: explicitly placing weights in socket-local DRAM via NUMA-aware memory allocation, and binding computations to the corresponding cores via NUMA-aware thread scheduling.

While mainstream frameworks for CPU inference, such as llama.cpp [6], deliver high baseline performance, they are not explicitly optimized for NUMA data locality. Recent work such as ArcLight [7] addresses this memory bottleneck through cross-NUMA tensor parallelism. However, because ArcLight is a custom inference engine written entirely in C++, it relies heavily on manual engineering and requires the model code to be meticulously rewritten to support different LLM architectures. In this work, we focus on lifting cross-NUMA Tensor Parallelism into PyTorch 2.0’s compiler ecosystem [8] to provide a PyTorch-native implementation. By extending the standard TorchInductor pipeline, our transformations remain entirely transparent to the user, requiring zero modifications to the model code, optimizer, or the inference loop.

papers.title: Recurrence and Uniqueness Criteria for Markov Processes from Moments of Integral-Type Functionals
papers.abstract: We investigate recurrence and uniqueness of continuous-time Markov chains using moments of integral-type functionals. Unlike the classical criteria from Chen (2004) and the Feller-Reuter criterion, we develop general unified conditions for recurrence and uniqueness of Markov processes based on moments of integral-type functionals. The associated criteria follow directly from these conditions whenever the mean functionals can be expressed explicitly. As applications, explicit recurrence and uniqueness criteria are derived for single-birth, single-death, and birth-death processes on trees.

authors.name: Ling-Di Wang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Experimental Hematology

papers.title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
papers.abstract: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.

papers.title: Gradient potential estimates for k-Hessian equations
papers.abstract: For $2\le k<n$, we prove pointwise gradient bounds for proper weak $k$-convex functions in terms of a local average and a Wolff potential of the full Hessian measure $F_k[u]$. The estimate yields local Lipschitz regularity for $F_k[u]=f$ with $f\in L^{n/k,1/k}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and for $F_k[u]=|Du|^p$ when $0<p<nk/(n-k)$. Both the Lorentz index $1/k$ and the upper bound on $p$ are sharp.

papers.title: Georeferenced Cross-View 3D Reconstruction from Ground and Satellite Images
papers.abstract: Georeferenced 3D reconstruction from ground images requires recovering not only the local scene geometry, but also localizing every camera center and 3D point in a geographic coordinate frame. Existing cross-view geo-localization methods are able to estimate the GPS coordinate of a single ground camera, but do not reconstruct dense 3D geometry, while recent feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction models predict point maps and camera poses only in a local coordinate frame. We introduce X-VGGT, a feed-forward cross-view geometry transformer that unifies these tasks by jointly processing a set of ground-level images and a georeferenced satellite image to predict ground-view camera poses, dense 3D point maps, and a scene-level transform parameterized by gravity, scale, yaw and translation. This transform projects the local reconstruction into the satellite plane, resulting in the geo-registration of all ground images with the georeferenced satellite image. We further propose an evaluation protocol for this joint task and show that, across multiple cross-view datasets, X-VGGT produces accurate georeferenced reconstructions and outperforms prior cross-view geo-localization and multi-view 3D reconstruction models.

papers.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based molecular docking requires learning a corrective score field across a broad corruption distribution, yet individual pose errors can differ substantially in their structural consequences. This creates a post-training conflict between preserving broad score-field coverage and concentrating supervision on corrections that appear more relevant to docking geometry. Using DiffDock, a fixed-budget study compares broad continuation with torsional supervision focused on Cartesian consequence or conditional target consistency, and with a broad/focused mixture. Evaluation separates fixed score fidelity, generated-pose quality, best-of-10 sampling capacity, and confidence-selected Top-1 docking performance. At <5 Angstrom, broad continuation had the highest mean Top-1 success among trained policies, and focused or mixed supervision showed no consistent advantage under the tested budget. The starting model had better fixed score fidelity, whereas the evaluated broad-continuation model had higher mean Top-1 success with the same aggregate best-of-10 recovery. Focusing supervision on structurally consequential or more consistently specified corrections did not consistently improve returned-pose success over broad continuation.

papers.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $\pi_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.

authors.name: Masayoshi Tomizuka
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Explicit bounds for the number of solutions to Roth-type inequalities over adelic curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide an upper bound on the number of a special system of Roth-type Diophantine inequalities over proper adelic curves. By refining the technique from previous work, we successfully eliminate the large-height restriction on the solutions. Furthermore, the constraints on the parameters within the inequality are further relaxed. We also give a constructive quantitative generalization of the Vojta-Dolce-Zucconi system, replacing compactness-based extraction by a discrete pigeonhole argument and a finite grid partition, so that the resulting bound has explicit dependence on the relevant parameters.

authors.name: YuXi Li
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Randomized Parallel Complexity of Weakly Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the minimum number of query rounds needed to find approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions, measured by the gradient of the Moreau envelope. Each round permits multiple simultaneous queries. In the stated parameter regime, the standard subgradient rate is optimal in sufficiently high dimensions, even for randomized algorithms making polynomially many parallel queries per round. We then show how the order structure of the real line enables faster search: a deterministic algorithm using only function values achieves logarithmic round complexity, with a further reduction through parallel queries. Matching lower bounds hold even when each query returns the entire subdifferential. Together, these results clarify the role of dimension in determining the benefits of parallel queries for weakly convex optimization.

papers.title: LABBA: LLM-Assisted Behavioral Biometric Authentication
papers.abstract:
Behavioral biometrics have emerged as a promising complement to traditional physiological biometrics by leveraging dynamic human characteristics. These modalities offer advantages including continuous authentication, inherent liveness detection, and greater resistance to credential theft and other spoofing attacks. However, existing systems remain limited in adaptability, contextual awareness, and semantic reasoning as they primarily rely on similarity metrics, static thresholds, or supervised classifiers. As a result, they often struggle with real-world conditions such as behavioral variability, environmental changes, contextual changes, and adversarial manipulations.
  To address these limitations, we systematically integrate LLM-based contextual reasoning into behavioral biometric authentication. LLMs provide capabilities in contextual inference, sequential reasoning, multimodal understanding, and adaptive decision-making. Building on these strengths, we integrate a lightweight LLM-based reasoning module with a novel phone-blowing behavioral biometric technique to develop a context-aware authentication framework. To this end, we first collect blow-acoustic signals from participants and systematically extract spectral and temporal features. These features are aggregated and converted into comparable similarity representations, using either discrete rule-based categories or continuous normalized scores, which are transformed into structured prompts through prompt engineering.
  We experimentally evaluate the proposed framework using blow-acoustic data collected from 50 participants under diverse behavioral and contextual conditions. The proposed framework achieves 99.46% and 99.38% authentication accuracy in the rule-based and score-based modes, respectively, outperforming its non-LLM counterpart while maintaining strong robustness under dynamic real-world conditions.

authors.institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design

papers.title: Tusn\'ady's problem and online two-sample thinning
papers.abstract:
We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusn\'ady's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample.
  We apply this geometric estimate to online thinning of two independent samples of size $n$ from an unknown common distribution, where observations must be kept or discarded upon arrival. For every fixed dimension $k\ge 1$ and expected deletion budget $\rho n$, with $0<\rho<2$, we prove that the minimax expected prefix discrepancy over lower orthants is $\Theta_{k,\rho}((\log n)^{k+1/2})$. In dimension one, the optimal terminal discrepancy is instead $\Theta_\rho((\log\log n)^{3/2})$, giving a sharp separation between the prefix and terminal objectives. For $k\ge 2$, we obtain terminal bounds differing by a factor of $\log n$.
  The lower bounds are based on Gaussian small-ball estimates for box-incidence matrices, while the upper bounds use stationary Metropolis thinning and, in one dimension, a terminal cancellation procedure.

papers.title: The Moving Frontier: How the National Justice Project Is Using Digital Technology to Expand Access to Justice
papers.abstract: Over the past three decades, technological advances have assisted individuals to gain access to legal information, enhance the efficiency of legal services, and streamline dispute resolution. More recently, the proliferation of generative artificial intelligence has reinforced this emphasis on firm-level productivity, with commercial legal practice increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence tools to automate document creation and optimise case management. While commercial technology focuses on productivity, community organisations are exploring how artificial intelligence can level the playing field for marginalised communities. Far less attention has been given to free, direct-to-consumer legal technologies, as these models are often unprofitable. Consequently, justice technology scholarship has overlooked a distinct class of technology: digital reporting platforms that enable people to record their experiences of harm, while simultaneously aggregating those accounts into a body of evidence capable of supporting advocacy, institutional accountability, and law reform. Crucially, experiences of discrimination and administrative abuse are often dismissed by oversight bodies as individual grievances. To understand the transformative potential of these platforms, this article asks two questions. First, how can digital reporting close the knowledge and power gap for marginalised communities interacting with the legal system? Second, how can these tools collect evidence to hold institutions accountable, drive change and contribute to a more just society?

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Coupling Photoionization & Multi-Frequency Radiation Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We use machine learning (ML) to couple photoionization microphysics to radiation hydrodynamic simulations of line-driven winds. ML models are trained on outputs from the photoionization code XSTAR to predict the line-driving force multiplier as a function of gas ionization, optical depth, and the blackbody temperature of the irradiating spectral energy distribution (SED). We implement the trained models within Athena++, enabling rapid runtime evaluation of the radiative acceleration without directly solving the photoionization problem during the hydrodynamic evolution. We find that random forest models provide the highest accuracy and reproduce the force multipliers over a three-dimensional parameter space more accurately, and with less training data, than traditional precomputed tables using trilinear interpolation. Because the framework treats the force multiplier as a function of the evolving local SED, it can be generalized to more complex radiation fields and arbitrary spectral shapes. More broadly, this work demonstrates how ML can serve as a computational framework for embedding expensive microphysical calculations within large-scale dynamical simulations.

papers.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
papers.abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $\Lambda$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $\Lambda$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.

papers.title: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters
papers.abstract: Many real-world applications, such as numerical weather prediction or wildfire tracking, involve modeling highly nonlinear dynamical systems that are chaotic and influenced by various sources of uncertainty. To improve model prediction accuracy and reduce such uncertainties, data assimilation (DA) combines the dynamical model with partial, noisy observations to estimate the evolution of the system's state. Doing so depends on solving the optimal filtering problem: computing the conditional distribution of a hidden state given a sequence of observations. Classical approaches fail along three distinct axes: Kalman-based methods assume Gaussian posteriors and produce biased estimates under nonlinear observation operators; particle-based methods represent distributions with weighted samples and collapse in high dimensions due to the curse of dimensionality; and kernel-based methods move beyond discrete particle representations but cannot maintain their density approximation affordably as dimension grows. The Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) avoids all three constraints by encoding the filtering density in a score function and approximating that score with a training-free Monte Carlo estimator, enabling stable filtering in high-dimensional, chaotic systems. This survey traces EnSF's mathematical foundations, establishes it as the state of the art for non-Gaussian, high-dimensional filtering, and examines fourteen extensions that expand its operational reach. Twelve of the fourteen extensions preserve this training-free Monte Carlo estimator at the core of the update, with only two departing from it to achieve planetary-scale deployment.

papers.intro:
Accurate forecasting of chaotic physical systems, from predicting hurricane tracks and wildfire spread to calibrating global climate simulations, requires continuously tracking a hidden state from noisy, partial observations. This is the central task of data assimilation, which fuses observational data with dynamical models to maintain accurate estimates of evolving systems as new data arrives. Computing the best estimate exactly is analytically intractable in all but the simplest settings, so every practical method must decide how to represent the uncertainty in the state and how to update that representation as new observations arrive. These two choices determine what a method can do and where it structurally fails.

These two choices determine what a method can do and where it structurally fails.

Two families of approximation methods have dominated the field for decades, and each achieves some of three properties a filtering method needs: non-Gaussian expressiveness, scalability to high dimensions, and affordability as posterior complexity grows. Kalman-based filters represent the filtering density as a Gaussian, which enables analytic updates that scale efficiently to very high dimensions and remain cheap to maintain regardless of posterior complexity [15, 20, 26, 27], but this Gaussian representation fails structurally whenever the true posterior is non-Gaussian. Particle-based filters represent the density as a set of weighted samples, which captures arbitrary non-Gaussian structure [14, 16], but under high-dimensional, strongly coupled observations, the number of samples required grows exponentially with dimension, making particle filters both unscalable and unaffordable in practice [43]. This is the ceiling that classical filtering could not escape, and it is the organizing question of this survey.

This is the ceiling that classical filtering could not escape, and it is the organizing question of this survey.

EnSF addresses this issue by building upon two ideas. The first is rooted in the theory of backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs), originally developed in stochastic control and later brought into filtering [7, 37, 38]. This lineage established that running a stochastic process backward in time extracts the distributional information the filtering update requires, with a martingale correction term keeping the backward evolution uniquely solvable, and it culminated in the kernel mixture representation this survey adopts as its BSDE filter [3]. The second is rooted in score based generative models [44], which showed how to generate samples from a target distribution by running a stochastic process backward in pseudo time instead of physical time. A forward diffusion process maps the target distribution to a simple reference distribution in finite pseudo time, typically a standard Gaussian, and the reverse process starts from that fixed reference and recovers the target. This removes the expensive problem specific terminal conditions that made filtering based on BSDEs computationally prohibitive [11].

The second is rooted in score based generative models [44], which showed how to generate samples from a target distribution by running a stochastic process backward in pseudo time instead of physical time. A forward diffusion process maps the target distribution to a simple reference distribution in finite pseudo time, typically a standard Gaussian, and the reverse process starts from that fixed reference and recovers the target. This removes the expensive problem specific terminal conditions that made filtering based on BSDEs computationally prohibitive [11].

The Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) builds on these two insights into a practical filtering algorithm [12]. Rather than storing the filtering density as a parametric Gaussian or particles that directly represent the density, EnSF encodes it in the score function, which is the gradient of the log-density with respect to the state. EnSF uses a reverse-time stochastic differential equation guided by this score to generate posterior samples at each assimilation step. Importantly, EnSF approximates the score through a closed-form training-free Monte Carlo estimator that requires no neural network retraining between steps, resolving the primary computational bottleneck of earlier score-based filters and enabling stable filtering in very high dimensional systems, such as those with one million state dimensions [12].

This survey traces the mathematical foundations and development of EnSF and examines the framework it has generated. Following a critical analysis of classical methods, the paper examines fourteen extensions of EnSF, organized as five acts that test whether EnSF’s core mechanism, once established, can absorb escalating operational demands without needing to change. The acts progress from improving the algorithm itself to testing whether the improved mechanism holds on harder states and forecasting problems. They then reach the point where the mechanism requires modification, and finally where its training-free property is given up for planetary-scale deployment. By characterizing every method according to how it represents and updates the filtering density, the survey establishes EnSF as the state of the art for non-Gaussian high-dimensional filtering, escaping the tradeoff between non-Gaussian expressiveness, scalability, and affordable density representation that constrained every classical approach.

papers.title: Prediction of antimagnon-polarons with intrinsic momentum-space level attraction
papers.abstract: Propagating hybrid quasiparticles formed by magnons and phonons (magnon-polarons) or photons (magnon-polaritons) typically exhibit level repulsion in momentum space. Level attraction, by contrast, requires an anti-phase channel and has so far been restricted to zero-dimensional systems mediated by dissipative baths. Here we predict the antimagnon-polaron in a continuous magnetoelastic medium, which inherently exhibits momentum-space level attraction. The spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-stabilized antimagnon precesses with opposite handedness, directly reversing the magnetoelastic coupling without requiring an external environment. This intrinsic attraction yields a distinctive 0/{\pi} phase-locked simultaneous growth. Micromagnetic simulations confirm this picture, revealing that the SOT-controlled balance between gain and damping drives a collective instability. This ultimately enables a continuously tunable, dc-pumped, single-frequency phonon laser, establishing a novel route for coherent acoustic emission.

papers.title: Global existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows with large initial data and vacuum
papers.abstract: For periodic initial data that allow vacuum, we establish the global-in-time existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows, under the condition that the bulk viscosity coefficient is sufficiently large and a geometric angular constraint is imposed on the initial direction field. Our results remain valid for arbitrarily large initial energy. Furthermore, under appropriate additional assumptions imposed on the pressure, we also establish the uniqueness of the constructed solutions.

authors.name: Qiao Liu
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: CountScan: Simultaneous Lower Bounds on Historical Watermark Matches over All Text Intervals
papers.abstract: A provider holding a watermark key may audit an external document and choose passages after reading it. A bound computed for a fixed passage is not valid for a passage chosen after seeing the evidence. One remedy splits the evidence between selection and validation. We take the other route and make the statement hold for every interval at once. CountScan gives finite-sample lower bounds on the number of retained historical watermark matches, simultaneously over all text intervals and count thresholds. Its validity rests on one condition: given the auditor's information, the pivots of positions that are not history matches are conditionally super-uniform. This condition holds when generation uses the key only through the Gumbel-max rule and editors have no access to the key, so the guarantee covers edits that depend on the generated text when the calibrators are nonincreasing. Simultaneity raises the threshold by the logarithm of the document length; for a long interval this costs about that logarithm divided by the critical evidence value, in certified tokens. We give a finite-length expansion of the certified proportion, finite-sample rates for two-level rules with lower bounds of the same order within a pivot-only class, and an upper bound over a calibrator class. On pre-registered holdouts with OPT and Qwen base models at temperature one, CountScan certifies substantial counts; under heavy random edits it remains valid but loses most of its power.

papers.title: Solving Linear Programs in the Matrix Multiplication Time
papers.abstract: We give a randomized algorithm for feasible bounded-box linear programs with $n$ variables and $d\le n=O(d)$ linearly independent equality constraints. For additive accuracy $\epsilon$, its expected running time is $O((n^\omega+n^2\log n)\log(1/\epsilon))$, where $\omega$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. This answers the matrix-multiplication-time open question posted in Song's Ph.D. thesis [Son19] in this setting.

authors.name: Zhao Song
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space endowed with a Finsler metric obtained from a Minkowski metric by a conformal deformation. We first derive the conformal transformation formulas for the fundamental tensor, the Cartan tensor, and the Chern connection of the conformally related Finsler metrics. Based on these formulas, we express the anisotropic mean curvature in the Gaussian space in terms of the corresponding anisotropic mean curvature with respect to the original Minkowski metric, and derive the associated evolution equation. Finally, we establish the short-time existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions by reformulating the geometric evolution equation as a strictly parabolic quasilinear partial differential equation.

papers.title: Universal Dimension Formula for Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $3r+1$
papers.abstract: We prove that Schumaker's lower bound gives the dimension of $S_{3r+1}^r(\Delta)$ for every nondegenerate triangulation $\Delta$ of a polygonal disk in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and every integer $r\ge3$. After accounting for the local vertex contributions, we reduce the remaining dimension defect to compatible vertex functionals. Apolarity associates a unique polynomial with each face, and compatibility forces differences of adjacent face polynomials to contain powers of both endpoint forms. We eliminate the leading residual coefficient using Hermite relations when $r$ is odd and an additional coefficient comparison when $r$ is even. A uniform induction then raises the endpoint powers until all face differences vanish; the zero boundary face potentials imply that every vertex functional vanishes and the global defect is zero. Together with the known cases $r=1,2$ and Hong's higher-degree theorem, this yields the dimension formula for all $r\ge1$ and $d\ge3r+1$.

authors.name: Jiansong Deng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models
papers.abstract: When a language model chooses a number between 1 and 30, every integer in the range is valid, yet the model can favor particular answers. We use numerical choice to study how preference is processed across layers and tokens. Perturbation probing and gradient attribution nominate neurons for activation interventions. In a selected Qwen3-4B case, a pre-answer edit changes 17 to 15 while both runs first emit 1. After the edit ends, selective cache and attention-output replacements trace part of its continuing influence on the second digit. Replacing one attention head's output or the other heads' outputs jointly produces similar immediate readout contributions; both interventions restore 17 but have different final log-odds effects on 7 versus 5. Holding later multilayer perceptron (MLP) outputs at their values from the edited run without either replacement reduces this effect gap from 0.119 to 0.0025 nat. Later computation therefore changes how similar local contributions affect the continuation. Retrospective estimates across eighteen contexts capture much of the probability movement but miss the selected answer switch. Prompt tests also separate influence from answer changes: one held-out prompt retains influence without switching, and only one of twelve fresh wordings qualifies for the reader/MLP test; there, joint MLP clamping again reduces the gap between the two reader effects while the answer remains 17. These results use numerical choice as a controlled case for studying persistent state and conditional downstream processing; they do not establish the origin or a complete circuit of natural numerical preference.

papers.title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification is essential for clinical deployment of cancer diagnosis models, yet neural networks and variational Gaussian process methods can produce overconfident predictions, particularly under the distribution shifts that arise when models trained at one hospital are applied at another. We present a scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification (GPC) framework that operates on frozen pathology foundation model embeddings (Phikon) and combines accelerated Randomly Pivoted Cholesky (RPCholesky) for low-rank kernel factorization, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) with non-centered parameterization for posterior sampling, and a pivots-as-inducing-points scheme for prediction. This makes HMC posterior sampling in the low-rank latent representation tractable at N approximately 300,000 training points, enabling HC-based low-rank GPC on substantially larger datasets than prior MCMC-based demonstrations. We evaluate on two histopathology benchmarks for breast cancer metastasis detection: PCam and CAMELYON17-WILDS, where the latter tests calibration under hospital-level distribution shift. Compared to stochastic variational GP and neural network baselines, our method improves calibration and predictive performance - reducing expected calibration error by up to 88% and false negative rate by up to 90% - with the largest gains appearing under distribution shift, suggesting that HMC-based posterior sampling provides more trustworthy uncertainty estimates for cross-site pathology classification.

authors.name: Yunru Zheng
authors.institution: Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Dark-State Coherent Control of Excitons in TMD Monolayers: A Reduced Intravalley Lindblad Framework for WSe$_2$
papers.abstract: Dark-state coherence in driven three-level systems underlies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP). Their performance depends on the coupling topology: in a ladder ($\Xi$) scheme the coherence can bypass a lossy intermediate state, whereas in a $V$ scheme it is carried by two excited states that both decay. We develop a topology-resolved Lindblad framework for driven three-level excitonic manifolds at fixed center-of-mass momentum, in which a single exciton couples to phonons, the radiation field and a dilute exciton gas. The $\Xi$ and $V$ manifolds are selected from the exciton spectrum by systematically screening optical brightness, intra-excitonic dipole strength and state compactness, making the selection reproducible and transferable to other materials. Within this framework, in the $\Xi$ manifold of hBN-encapsulated WSe$_2$, a weak optical pulse, preceded by a terahertz pulse in the counterintuitive STIRAP order, converts the excitation it creates into an optically dark exciton by dark-state following, while the lossy bright intermediate exciton stays nearly empty. The conversion is limited by emission from that intermediate state rather than by non-adiabatic coupling, and is controlled by a single adiabaticity parameter of the terahertz leg. The exchange mean field of the exciton gas shifts the two-photon resonance by more than the conversion tolerates at moderate densities; the center of the cascade transparency window provides an in situ calibration, and we identify the control strengths at which it is true EIT rather than Autler--Townes splitting. The $V$ manifold loses its coherence on the radiative timescale and serves as the unprotected reference. These results provide a minimal, material-specific baseline for dark-state coherent control of excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors in the radiative limit.

authors.name: Mauricio Martinez
authors.institution: Colombian Corporation for Agricultural Research - AGROSAVIA

papers.title: Object ideals and idempotent completeness
papers.abstract: We construct an idempotent complete Frobenius exact category with an idempotent complete stable category in which a complete ideal cotorsion pair of object ideals induces a cotorsion pair of objects that fails to be complete. This gives a negative answer to the question of Fu, Guil Asensio, Herzog and Torrecillas under idempotent completeness. The construction uses a lemma on dense triangulated subcategories and an example of Bondarko and Sosnilo in which a weight structure fails to extend to the idempotent completion. The induced cotorsion pair is hereditary, and every object admits an ordinary precover from its left class and an ordinary preenvelope into its right class. We characterize which objects admit special precovers and which admit special preenvelopes.

papers.title: Cognitive Tours: Making Understanding a Deliverable in AI-Assisted Development
papers.abstract: Generative AI and agentic coding are accelerating software development, leading to concerns about technical debt. But two less visible forms of debt, cognitive debt and intent debt, are emerging as key risks to software health. Cognitive debt is the absence or erosion of a team's shared understanding where no one can confidently explain how a system works or predict the impact of a change. Intent debt is the lack of clearly articulated goals, constraints, and rationale that explain what the system is for and guide how it should evolve. This paper presents Cognitive Tours, a tool designed to mitigate and repair cognitive and intent debt. Cognitive Tours is a web-based prototype for creating and following curated paths connecting user needs, design decisions, code, tests, and open questions. AI-assisted skills help audit existing waypoints and tours for possible problems or staleness and suggest candidates for new ones; humans decide what matters, verify relationships, and construct the narrative. This division of work deliberately preserves productive friction: the sensemaking involved in selecting, explaining, and revising a tour, which is intended to foster and share understanding. Our demonstration uses a tour of Cognitive Tours itself to introduce the tool and illustrate its design decisions and interaction mechanisms. A proposed evaluation agenda concludes the paper. A demo is available at https://cognitive-tours-demo.vercel.app/

papers.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods for Unbounded Problems
papers.abstract: Last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods have attracted significant attention as practical implementations typically return the last iterate instead of an average of the iterates. In this paper, we study two approaches for analyzing the last-iterate convergence of proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods without bounded domain or bounded variance assumptions, where black-box variational inference serves as a running example. Under two related assumptions relaxing the bounded variance, we show near-optimal anytime rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ for the last iterate. Moreover, when the horizon $T$ is known, we remove the logarithmic factor and obtain the optimal order $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$, matching the order known under bounded variance or bounded domain assumptions.

papers.title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue
papers.abstract: For humans, referential disambiguation is a collaborative process involving clarification questions asked when they will meaningfully change the outcome. However, large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be biased toward premature answering, preferring definite single-turn responses over more clarification exchanges. In this paper, we study the problem of "strategic clarification" -- asking clarification questions in a reference game when their answers will narrow the set of candidate referents. We construct a controlled test environment from the SIMMC 2.1 dataset that records how many questions each ambiguous reference needs to be successfully resolved, and examine how baseline LLM behavior and common post-training methods ask clarifying questions vs. attempt to answer the referent. We also propose BACE (Belief-Aware Critic with Epistemic tracking), a lightweight action chooser method on top of a frozen LM backbone, and show that BACE more consistently chooses the optimal number of clarifying questions than methods such as GRPO and ArCHer.

papers.title: A Deep-Learning Framework for the Generalized Emulation of Atmospheric Radiative Transfer at Microwave Frequencies
papers.abstract: This paper presents an application of machine learning to the problem of the computational expense of atmospheric radiative transfer calculations from physics-based models. While in recent studies individual emulators have been created that emulate certain radiative transfer schemes for different sensors, we show that a general framework can be applied to emulate the radiative transfer method itself. A fully connected deep neural network has been trained to predict top-of-atmosphere microwave radiances in all-sky conditions over various land, ocean and sea ice surfaces at all frequencies from 1 to 300 GHz, and for all incidence angles from 0 to 65 degrees. The reference models against which the emulator has been trained include an Eddington two-stream radiative transfer model for one-dimensional and pseudo-three-dimensional microwave brightness temperature simulations. This neural network architecture has also been separately trained to reproduce the explicit calculations of the Community Radiative Transfer Model (CRTM) for a single microwave imager. In all cases, the model architecture is successfully able predict microwave brightness temperatures by being trained directly on the optical properties of the atmosphere and surface and therefore directly emulating the radiative transfer method. Compared to the explicit schemes used to produce the training data, the GPU-enabled emulator is able to produce brightness temperature simulations more than three orders of magnitude faster and with a root-mean-squared-error less than 0.0348 K, 0.0531 K, and 0.0246 K against the independent test data for the two Eddington models and CRTM, respectively. Additionally, preliminary training using a full 3D Monte Carlo scheme for high-resolution simulations shows promising results for the application of this method to "exact" radiative transfer methods, and these results are discussed in Section IV.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Extremizers and Convergence of the Euler-Lagrange Iteration for the Critical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Inequality
papers.abstract: Let $n \ge 3$, $2 \le \alpha < n$, and $1 < p,r < \infty$ satisfy $p^{-1}+r^{-1}=1+\alpha/n$. We prove uniqueness, up to common translations and dilations, of the normalized nonnegative extremizing pairs for the corresponding Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality. More generally, all positive finite-energy solutions of the Euler-Lagrange system belong to a single symmetry orbit. The proof compares two solutions at different relative scales. Total positivity of order two identifies the second eigenspace of an associated compact self-adjoint operator and forces each nonzero difference to change sign exactly once. The opposite orientations obtained at the two ends of the scale parameter then yield uniqueness. The same method proves radial nondegeneracy modulo dilation. We also establish strong convergence of the normalized alternating Euler-Lagrange iteration from every nonnegative, radially nonincreasing initial datum to a fixed extremizing pair, without rescaling the iterates. Square-root mass variables reduce the exclusion of several concentration profiles to a static spectral estimate and an energy-increment argument. The analysis includes sublinear exponents and the logarithmic borderline decay regimes.

papers.title: The probabilistic bound for perfect hashing is sharp only for binary alphabets
papers.abstract: We investigate the optimal asymptotic rate $R_q$ of perfect $q$-hash codes, a fundamental extremal problem in combinatorics, information theory, and computer science. Let $B_q=-\log_2(1-q!/q^q)/(q-1)$ denote the classical probabilistic lower bound. We prove that $R_q=B_q$ if and only if $q=2$, establishing an explicit strict improvement for every $q\ge3$ and settling the first assertion of a conjecture of Xing and Yuan (Combinatorica 43 (2023), 347--366). More significantly, we show that, for every $\eta>0$, $R_q\ge B_q+\exp(-(2+\eta)q)$ for all sufficiently large integers $q$. This improves the previously known increments of scale $\exp(-3q+O(\ln q))$ by an exponential factor. We also establish a structural limitation of the concatenation method. For pairwise uniform inner codes of subexponential length, the resulting rate bound exceeds $B_q$ by at most $\exp(-3q+o(q))$. Thus, exponentially long inner codes are necessary to achieve the new improvement scale within this framework. Our proofs combine Fourier analysis, high-dimensional simplex codes, additive permutation counts, and entropy bounds for hypergraph matchings. We further strengthen lower bounds from short inner codes and improve several known numerical estimates.

papers.title: Cognitive Bias Signatures in Search-Equipped LLM Agents: A Stage-Resolved Analysis
papers.abstract: Search can help LLM agents correct mistakes, but their starting conditions may shape which evidence they find and use. Drawing on cognitive-bias paradigms, we develop a controlled search harness to examine result order, records of prior work, and initial hypotheses while holding each question and document collection fixed. Matched controls distinguish order effects from differences in document composition and the effects of failed work from context length. Across 10 models and 1,000 synthetic search worlds, we track queries, retrieved documents, document openings, and final answers. Our comparisons suggest that final answers are more sensitive to initial evidence order during active search than when all evidence is supplied in full. Dead-end histories can reduce strategy switching relative to matched neutral histories, indicating an effect beyond context length. Under wrong hypotheses, stage measurements distinguish reduced retrieval or opening from errors that persist after counter-evidence is opened. Exploratory interventions show that opening counter-evidence more often can coincide with lower accuracy, while accuracy can improve with little change in opening.

papers.title: Two-row Schur times Schubert via parallel classes of positroid varieties
papers.abstract: Schubert structure constants are intersection numbers of Schubert varieties. Finding positive combinatorial formulas for these constants remains a major open problem. We resolve this problem when one of the indexing permutations corresponds to a two-row partition. Our approach uses increasing chains, introduced by Sottile for the one-row case, and builds on the skew Schubert functions studied by Bergeron and Sottile. The key step is to connect increasing chains and these functions with the parallel classes of positroid varieties.

authors.name: Tianyi Yu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Quadratic-Time Barriers from Self-Referential SAT
papers.abstract: Under the self-referential $K$-SAT exhaustive-search hypothesis (SRK-ESH), no uniform deterministic algorithm computes exact longest common subsequence or standard edit distance on binary strings in $O(n^{2-\eta})$ time for any fixed $\eta>0$, where $n$ is the longer sequence length. The same exclusion holds for one-dimensional dynamic time warping on $\{0,1,2,4,8\}$ with absolute-difference cost and for five-symbol dynamic time warping with the discrete metric. We derive Orthogonal Vectors hardness in polylogarithmic dimension by splitting the variables of the logarithmic-width source formula into two halves. Existing sequence reductions have polynomial overhead in the dimension. Their output lengths and construction times allow a fixed saving in the target exponent to yield a fixed proportional saving in the source exponent.

papers.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
papers.abstract: Self-consistency (SC) is a widely used decoding strategy for improving chain-of-thought reasoning, but it requires sampling many complete reasoning trajectories with a preset budget. Its efficient variants reduce the cost mainly by stopping full-trajectory sampling early or distributing the number of samples across questions. In this paper, we propose StepBack, a step-level error-localized resampling method for efficient test-time reasoning. Given a small set of draft trajectories, StepBack localizes likely first error positions using lightweight signals and then resamples the detected error step and its suffix, followed by majority answer voting. Empirically, StepBack matches the accuracy of SC on average across seven mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks, while reducing token usage by up to 41.26%. In addition, by nature, StepBack can be combined with adaptive inference methods such as Adaptive Consistency, further improving their inference-time efficiency.

papers.title: The second reconstruction transition for random graphs from 2-neighborhoods
papers.abstract: We prove that, with high probability, the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ is reconstructible up to isomorphism from the multiset of its rooted induced 2-neighborhoods whenever $p\geq n^{-3/4}(\log n)^3$. Together with the non-reconstructibility result of Johnston, Kronenberg, Roberts and Scott, our result locates the second reconstruction transition at the scale $p=n^{-3/4}$ up to polylogarithmic factors, resolving a question they posed. Our proof relies on a global rigidity argument exploiting 5-cycle constraints.

authors.name: Yiming Chen
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Polarization cross-talk from non-stationary sources of image jitter
papers.abstract: We generalize a previous formulation for the estimation of polarization cross-talk induced by atmospheric seeing to the case of image jitter that must be described as a non-stationary, and generally non-isotropic, random process. We demonstrate how the newly derived formalism converges towards the previous one in the limit of stationary random image jitter. In the case of non-stationary processes, we compare the predictions of the two formalisms, and illustrate the salient differences. For the sake of demonstration, we adopt for our analysis a specific example of power-spectral density derived from a circulant auto-correlation function, which describes a class of stationary random processes periodic over the length of the time series, and which we successively modified by the insertion of off-diagonal power spectral features at different frequencies in order to test the extended modeling framework for the estimation of polarization cross-talk.

authors.name: R. Casini
authors.institution: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

authors.name: A. G. de Wijn
authors.institution: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

papers.title: Constraining the timescale of activity in Mrk 1018
papers.abstract: We present analysis of an extended emission line region projected 3.77 kpc from the nucleus of the canonical changing-look AGN Mrk~1018, found in MUSE integral-field observations from the Close AGN Reference Survey. Emission-line ratios show that the region exhibits AGN ionisation but has a very low velocity dispersion, $77 \pm 1$ kms$^{-1}$, ruling out an ionised outflow. The lower limit on the light travel time is $12{,}300 \pm 2{,}300$ yr, implying that the nucleus has therefore been active for at least this long. This is much longer than the duration of either observed changing-look transition, which occurred over several years. This implies that Mrk 1018's multi-year variations are occurring within a longer term active phase.

authors.name: Scott M. Croom
authors.institution: International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research

papers.title: A First Look at Starlink Maritime on Cruise Ships
papers.abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite networks are reshaping maritime connectivity, offering much lower latency and higher capacity than traditional geostationary (GEO) links. As a single user terminal (UT) cannot serve hundreds to thousands of passengers, a cruise ship often deploys several UTs behind an onboard multi-WAN router for aggregated capacity and load balancing. Consequently, passenger connectivity depends not only on the satellite links but also on how the router distributes sessions among UTs. In this paper, we measure Starlink maritime connectivity on two cruise ships of different scales, Utopia of the Seas near the Bahamas in December 2025 and Silver Muse in the Adriatic Sea in July 2026, combining UT telemetry, inside-out measurements from a passenger device, and outside-in measurements from cloud servers near Starlink Points of Presence (PoPs). We find that the onboard network, rather than the satellite links, largely determines the passenger experience, as cruise lines rate limit each passenger device. Moreover, the public IP address of a passenger device changes not only at PoP handovers but also within the same PoP. Furthermore, while the country code reported by the UT reflects the maritime jurisdiction of the ship, the serving PoP follows neither this jurisdiction nor geographic proximity alone, suggesting factors beyond the distance-based PoP boundaries observed in Starlink aviation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of Starlink on commercial cruise ships, complementing prior land mobile and in-flight measurements.

authors.name: Jinwei Zhao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
papers.abstract: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks. Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%. Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.

papers.title: Inference after selection on randomized p-values
papers.abstract: We consider inference on parameters and hypotheses selected using p-values. We provide a simple procedure to decompose a p-value into two components, one for inference and one for selection, that are independent under the null hypothesis. To control the Type 1 error rate conditional on selection of the null hypothesis from randomized p-values, we develop tests motivated by the selective inference approaches of data thinning, fission, and carving. Unlike the typical application of these approaches, however, our tests only make use of the p-values rather than the full data. Furthermore, we construct confidence intervals that attain the nominal conditional coverage and corresponding estimators. In the context of the file drawer problem, the winner's curse, and sequential testing, we show that our proposals offer both theoretical and empirical advantages over existing randomized and non-randomized approaches. Lastly, we apply our methods for selective inference on genetic associations using publicly-available p-values from the UK Biobank.

papers.title: A Christov Integrating Factor Method for Approximating Rational PDE Solutions
papers.abstract: Rational solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) are notoriously difficult to approximate via spectral Fourier methods due to their algebraically slow decay rate. In this work we discuss approximating rational PDE solutions in a basis of orthogonal functions known as the Christov functions, allowing for the computation of its spectrum via the fast Fourier transform. An explicit fourth-order integrating factor method is derived. The effectiveness of the method is tested on several nonlinear PDEs. Relative to a straightforward pseudo-spectral approximation, the integrating factor method supports larger regions of stability resulting in a more efficient scheme.

papers.title: Simple Modules over Leavitt Path Algebras Generated by Indicator Functions on Paths
papers.abstract: Let E be an arbitrary graph, K a field, and D the set of boundary paths of E consisting of both infinite paths and finite paths ending at singular vertices. The space KD of K-valued functions on D is a right module over the Leavitt path algebra LK(E). For a non- empty set S ? D that is strongly connected and closed under adding and deleting initial segments, we study the submodule N_S = 1_S.LK(E) generated by the indicator function of S. Let S_0 be the set of vertices lying on the paths in S. We show that N_S is simple if and only if S contains no breaking vertex of the hereditary saturated set H = E0 nS0. In particular, when S contains only infinite paths or when E is a row- finite graph, NS is a simple module. Up to isomorphism, the simple module NS depends only on S_0. When S is an infinite set of paths, the simple module NS is neither graded nor projective. The left module LK(E)1_S, obtained by twisting the action through the involution of LK(E), is simple exactly when NS is, and, when S is infinite, it is not isomorphic to any of the Chen simple modules. For the rose graph R_n with n ? 2 petals, we show that LK(R_n)1_S is isomorphic to one of the twisted Chen modules constructed by Nam, Srivastava and Vien, and to none of the other simple modules in their list. Moreover, when S is not a single vertex, the simple module NS is finitely presented if and only if only finitely many edges of E have both source and range in S_0; in particular, every simple module N_S is finitely presented when E is a finite graph. Finally, we determine when the analogous module generated by an indicator function over the Cohn path algebra CK(E) is simple. 1.

authors.name: Elizabeth Pacheco
authors.institution: Prefeitura Municipal de Campos dos Goytacazes

papers.title: Three-critical hypergraphs of maximum local edge connectivity two
papers.abstract: For a hypergraph \(G\), let \(\chi(G)\) denote its chromatic number and \(\lambda(G)\) the maximum, over pairs of distinct vertices, of the minimum size of an edge cut separating the pair. A hypergraph is \(3\)-critical if its chromatic number is three and every proper subhypergraph is two-colorable. In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of the \(3\)-critical hypergraphs with \(\lambda(G)\le2\). We prove that these are precisely the hypergraphs generated from ordinary odd cycles and an explicit family of labeled-tree hypergraphs by admissible Toft splits. This characterization includes a necessary and sufficient condition for a prescribed split to preserve \(\lambda\le2\). The condition involves only cuts in the first factor and the two traces on the split edge. More generally, we establish an exact cut formula for splits at degree-\(k\) vertices of \((k+1)\)-critical hypergraphs, for every \(k\ge2\). We further prove that the smallest member of this critical class outside the family generated by hyperwheels and both forms of the Haj\'os join has eight vertices and is unique up to isomorphism. Together, these results resolve two issues left open by Schweser, Stiebitz, and Toft in \emph{Journal of Combinatorics} (2022): the characterization of hypergraphs with \(\lambda(G)=2\) and \(\chi(G)=3\), and whether hyperwheels and Haj\'os joins suffice to generate all \(3\)-critical hypergraphs in this connectivity range.

papers.title: Clique partitions and distinct color sets in list colorings
A Gingerbread House for LLM Agents: Source-Planned Honeypots That Lure Autonomous Attackers into an Isolated Shadow
papers.abstract: LLM agents can exploit web vulnerabilities fast enough that patching may come too late. Deception against such agents has mostly lured them away from a real target that stays reachable. We study a different arrangement: an LLM defender plans a static honeypot from the application's source, and a router sends every later request of a client it confirms as an attacker, including a working exploit, to an isolated shadow copy. We compare no defence, this static plan, and an augmented configuration with a runtime LLM responder and further router rules, graded by the benchmark's own grader on the real target and, for ARTEX, also on the shadow. On the 40 critical CVE-Bench tasks the static plan cut real compromise from 26/40 to 5/40 for Claude Opus 4.8 and from 20/40 to 0/40 (31 valid runs) for the ARTEX attack framework. On 20 new tasks not used in the design, ARTEX went from 15/20 to 0/20. In about half of the deception-arm runs ARTEX's exploit succeeded on the shadow while the real target stayed intact: the defence moved a working exploit rather than stopping it, and the remaining risk lies in requests that reach the real target before confirmation. ARTEX reported a planted fake secret as genuine on 30 of the 120 deception-arm tasks, five times in a report that labelled another item a decoy. With ARTEX's real compromise at zero in both deception configurations, they did not differ significantly on the remaining outcomes, a comparison that does not isolate the responder.

papers.title: Anti-ribbon shaped Young diagram decomposition
papers.abstract: We introduce a sliding procedure on diagrams which splits the standard Young tableaux of a corner-crossed diagram, in particular of a skew shape, along a finite binary tree whose leaves are anti-ribbon diagrams. Combined with standardization, this yields a decomposition of semi-standard Young tableaux into tableaux of anti-ribbon shape, indexed by standard tableaux and governed by their descent sets. As applications, we obtain expansions of Schur functions and Schur multiple zeta functions in terms of their anti-ribbon type analogues; at the level of Schur functions, this is a tableau-level form of Gessel's fundamental quasisymmetric expansion.

papers.title: A Novel Asymmetric Distributed Voltage Regulation Scheme to Enhance the Utilization of Distributed Energy Resources
papers.abstract: Passive voltage regulation in distribution grids using distributed energy resources (DERs) is becoming the standard for feeder voltage management in both under-voltage and over-voltage scenarios. Their simple control, ease of implementation, and fast response make them ideal for distribution feeders with high-DER penetration. This paper proposes a novel distributed voltage control for DERs based on the voltage at the point of common coupling, inverter rating, and operating active power. The proposed control is designed to utilize feeder inverters efficiently to reduce the burden on the inverters in both under-voltage and over-voltage operations and increase the fairness in reactive power ($Q$) support in over-voltage operations. The proposed control is implemented in static and dynamic simulations of a real feeder to validate the performance. Results for the under-voltage scenario are also presented in the paper.

authors.name: Dan Moldovan
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.title: Kappa Classes on the KSBA Space of Stable Toric Pairs
papers.abstract: We study kappa classes on the normalization of the main component of the Koll\'ar--Shepherd-Barron--Alexeev(KSBA) moduli space of stable toric pairs. Using a toric model obtained by a lattice modification, we compute all kappa classes on the moduli space by giving a combinatorial formula for their intersection numbers with all torus-invariant cycles. In particular, we identify the first normalized kappa class with the GKZ polarization of the toric variety corresponding to the secondary polytope. For interval configurations, we also obtain a closed formula for all top intersection products of normalized kappa classes.

authors.name: Byeol Han
authors.institution: Eulji University Uijeongbu Eulji Medical Center

papers.title: The Approximation Property without the Bounded Approximation Property in a Separable Banach Space and Its Dual
papers.abstract:
We investigate whether a dual Banach space with the approximation property (AP) must necessarily have the bounded approximation property (BAP). Using a quantitative renorming theorem for the space of absolutely summable sequences, we establish a direct-sum construction yielding a negative answer.
  More precisely, we construct a separable Banach space (X) such that both (X) and its dual (X^*) have the approximation property, while neither space has the bounded approximation property. The construction uses a sequence of equivalent renormings of (\ell_1) with increasingly restrictive finite-dimensional approximation bounds. By assembling these spaces through a (c_0)-direct sum, we obtain a dual space whose approximation property is preserved, but whose approximation constants cannot be uniformly bounded.
  We establish the required transfer principles, including the preservation of approximation bounds under complemented coordinate projections and the descent of the bounded approximation property from a dual space to its predual. We also provide an explicit complex-scalar version of the construction.
  The argument separates the external quantitative renorming input from the direct-sum construction and its functional-analytic consequences. In particular, the resulting example demonstrates that the approximation property of a dual space does not imply its bounded approximation property, even when the predual is separable and both spaces possess the approximation property.

authors.name: Ma Yicen
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Overholonomicity of Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
