papers.abstract: We prove that $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over smooth $k((t))$-varieties are overholonomic and construct the triangulated category of overholonomic complexes of Frobenius type which is stable under six operations and contains overconvergent $F$-isocrsytals.

authors.name: Yuanmin Liu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Cross-Family Mode Coupling and Localization Reversal in Phononic Crystal Defect Dimers
papers.abstract: Defects in phononic crystals confine elastic vibrations within bandgaps, enabling waveguiding, sensing, and energy harvesting. Coupling defects offers control over the spatial distribution of vibration, but how interactions between nearby modal families determine defect preference remains unclear. We examine localization reversal in dimers whose single defect supports a nearby $B_1$ singlet and $E$ doublet: softening one defect shifts a continued modal branch toward its unchanged partner. In off-axis and diagonal layouts, this reversal accompanies family exchange, with opposing $B_1$ and $E$ contributions to the defect-mass difference nearly cancelling at the threshold. Deleting cross-family stiffness and mass blocks removes reversal, while omitting cross-family observable terms at fixed states preserves it, identifying modal redistribution as the dominant mechanism. At the off-axis softening endpoint, independent channels predict the opposite preferred defect despite a $0.16\%$ frequency difference from the full-order solution. Nominal operators retaining the complete singlet-doublet space predict selected softening-branch thresholds with errors below $1.1\%$ against independent full-order sign brackets, without fitting detuned trajectories. These results link localization reversal to modal-family exchange and physical defect-mass balance, and show that frequency agreement alone does not guarantee localization accuracy.

papers.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone
papers.abstract: How would we know whether a machine truly understands the world? We argue that one key capability is \textit{observational theory learning}: acquiring reusable theories from pure observations and applying them to new situations. Current visual reasoning benchmarks focus primarily on the latter, presenting each task as a few-shot puzzle grouped by a common rule. We introduce BabyTheorist, a benchmark for controlled training and evaluation of observational theory learning. BabyTheorist generates continual streams of before-after visual observations from hidden compositional programs; during training, learners see only the resulting transitions, with no program labels, task identities, or support sets. To support theory learning and evaluation, BabyTheorist controls the program language, a curriculum over program complexity, recurring frequent subprograms, and a continual train-test protocol with level skipping. Seven representative baselines plateau well below ceiling, with the gap widening as the curriculum advances---evidence that BabyTheorist isolates a capability current program-learning approaches do not yet address.

authors.name: Doojin Baek
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Junyeob Baek
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Exact $\ell_p$-CVP via Euclidean SVP in Polynomial Space
papers.abstract:
We give a randomized, rank-preserving reduction from exact $\ell_p$-CVP to exact Euclidean SVP for every integer $p\ge2$. For rational inputs of bit length $\ell$ on full-rank lattices $L\subset\mathbb R^N$, the reduction uses $(Cp)^N\poly(p,\ell)$ oracle calls and additional bit operations, where $C$ is an absolute constant. It uses $\poly(p,\ell)$ working space outside the oracle, and all oracle queries have rank $N$ and $\poly(p,\ell)$ bit complexity.
  For $p=2$, the reduction transfers polynomial-space exact SVP algorithms to exact CVP with $2^{O(N)}\poly(\ell)$ time overhead. Instantiating it with the SVP algorithms of Kannan and of Feng, Gao and Liu yields randomized polynomial-space CVP algorithms running in time $N^{N/(2e)+o(N)}$ and $N^{N/(4e)+o(N)}$, respectively. For every fixed integer $p\ge3$, the same reduction yields exact $\ell_p$-CVP algorithms for arbitrary rational targets either in randomized time and space $2^{O(N)}$, or in randomized time $N^{N/(4e)+o(N)}$ and polynomial space. These algorithmic bounds are up to polynomial factors in $\ell$.
  The reduction performs local search sequentially over the cosets of \(2L\), where \(L\) is the input lattice, while tracking the excess of the current objective value over the optimum. Within a coset containing a closest vector, midpoint inequalities bound the unknown correction in terms of this excess, which in turn allows us to construct many short corrections that reduce the excess bound by a factor of four. A counting argument shows that these improving corrections form a sufficiently large fraction of the lattice points in a known search region, and a sparsification-based sampler assigns sufficiently large probability to every nonzero vector in that region, using at most one SVP call per sample. For \(p\ge3\), the same framework is extended using a diagonal weighted norm computed from the current point.

papers.title: Binding Paraphrased Instructions to Encountered Objects in sLLM Agents under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: Reliable deployment of LLM agents requires grounding diverse user expressions in their environments. Although RL-finetuned smaller large language model (sLLM) agents rival larger prompted LLMs on embodied tasks, their robustness to instruction paraphrases remains unclear. We introduce ALFWorld-Para to evaluate this robustness under controlled paraphrases, revealing 21-52% declines in success rates (SRs), predominantly driven by object synonyms. Despite retaining knowledge of synonym referents, agents often fail to take the corresponding objects even after observing them, exposing a gap between referential knowledge and object binding. Partial observability further complicates binding, as referents may remain unseen or have already been encountered under different labels. To address this challenge, we propose BINDIntent, a training-free framework that probabilistically binds referring expressions to observed labels using semantic proximity and estimated persistence against unseen candidates. Without additional training or LLM calls, BINDIntent improves synonym-paraphrase success of RL-finetuned sLLMs by 17.5-49.1 percentage points (pp) with only 0.4 ms of CPU overhead per step. It also raises GiGPO-7B's overall SR from 61.8% to 77.4%, surpassing a prompted 24B LLM. Code and benchmark are available at https://github.com/cau-hai-lab/ALFWorld-Para.

papers.title: A Sequential Framework for Urban Drone Delivery: Network Design, Vehicle Sizing, and Energy and Cost Assessment
papers.abstract: A sequential engineering framework is presented for urban drone delivery, linking hub location, route planning, mission-specific vehicle sizing, and energy and operating cost assessment. Aggregate origin-destination demand is assumed known a priori. For each hub configuration, the maximum required link distance is minimized, and feasible routes that return to their departure hubs are generated. Route frequencies are determined using mixed-integer linear programming to satisfy delivery demand. The resulting range requirement guides motor-propeller selection and battery sizing to minimize vehicle takeoff mass. Flight distances and frequencies, cruise performance, and vehicle dimensions are combined to estimate monthly energy consumption, fleet size, hub area, staffing, and operating cost. The framework is applied to district-level Seoul delivery data. Increasing the number of hubs from one to four reduces the required range from 30.6 to 21.9 km and vehicle takeoff mass from 8.12 to 6.12 kg. Despite a 21.5% increase in total flight distance, monthly flight energy consumption decreases by 13.1%, from 15.2 to 13.2 MWh. Battery replacement is the largest vehicle-related operating expense, while operating cost per delivery increases from USD 1.18 to USD 2.20 because of higher rent and labor costs at the hubs. Among the designs evaluated, range-matched vehicles achieve the lowest operating cost in the two- and four-hub networks; a longer-range vehicle is least costly in the three-hub network. Sensitivity analyses further examine the effects of delivery demand and operating assumptions. The results demonstrate that reductions in vehicle mass and energy consumption do not necessarily lead to lower system operating cost.

authors.name: Seokhwan Lee
authors.institution: Korea Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Lagrangian Approach to Uniqueness for Active Scalars in Generalized Mean Oscillation Spaces
papers.abstract: We develop a unified Lagrangian framework for the uniqueness of weak solutions to a broad class of two-dimensional inviscid active scalar equations in generalized mean oscillation spaces. Under common structural assumptions on the Biot--Savart kernels, we identify mean oscillation spaces that ensure an Osgood condition for the velocity, and establish uniqueness in these classes. For the two-dimensional Euler equations, we establish uniqueness for vorticities whose mean oscillation grows mildly at small scales, extending beyond $\mathrm{BMO}$. For the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) and incompressible porous media (IPM) equations, we obtain uniqueness in spaces logarithmically rougher than $C^{0,1}$. We also obtain what are (to our knowledge) the strongest known uniqueness results for the $\alpha$-SQG equation, $0<\alpha<1$, in spaces logarithmically rougher than critical H\"older spaces $C^\alpha$. The framework also applies to various logarithmically perturbed models, yielding uniqueness in the corresponding sharp regularity classes. The proof combines a sharp regularity estimate for the velocity with a stability estimate for integral operators under measure-preserving rearrangements. This provides a single uniqueness argument for the entire family under common structural assumptions on the kernels.

papers.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
papers.abstract: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. In this paper, we propose EFXPLORER, a constrained exploration framework that maximizes exploration objectives subject to a constraint that preserves established task performance. We solve the resulting problem using an epigraph reformulation that introduces adaptive exploration budgets. This approach separates intrinsic rewards from task objectives and regulates exploration through task feasibility. To further encourage diverse and temporally extended exploration, we incorporate a successor distance-based intrinsic reward that captures long-horizon dependencies. Empirically, our method outperforms strong baselines and induces novel cooperative strategies across SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmark suites.

papers.title: Local Homological Mirror Symmetry
papers.abstract: Local mirror symmetry, originated from the work of Chiang-Klemm-Yau-Zaslow arXiv:9903053, indicated a potential relation between mirrors to a vector bundle and mirrors to its zero section. In this paper, we constructed a homological mirror to these local varieties and proved the corresponding Homological Mirror Symmetry statement. As an application, we constructed infinite families of exotic Weinstein sectors as mirrors to Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: Fields Generated by a Single Point on Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We study the finite extensions of a number field generated by a single point on an elliptic curve. We construct geometrically non-isomorphic elliptic curves with complex multiplication that generate the same collection of extensions, giving a negative answer to a question of Mazur and Rubin. For torsion-generated fields, we prove that inclusion of the collections up to finitely many exceptions implies isogeny over the ground field, and in the non-CM case even isomorphism. When all geometric endomorphisms are defined over the ground field, we characterize equality of the torsion-generated collections by the existence, for every prime $p$, of an isogeny over the ground field of degree prime to $p$. This condition also implies equality of the full collections of fields generated by a single point.

papers.title: Algebraic classification of single-field inflationary dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop an algebraic classification of canonical single-field inflationary dynamics using an exact depressed cubic equation for the inflaton velocity. Its root structure identifies a branch-swap boundary distinct from the limiting boundary of downhill motion, where ultra-slow-roll inflation naturally emerges. Independently, the conservation of momentum conjugate to the comoving curvature perturbation in the long-wavelength limit provides a criterion for the growth or decay of the gauge-invariant difference between comoving and uniform-density curvature perturbations. Combining these criteria, we construct a unified dynamical chart in terms of the Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, illustrating its applicability to constant-roll inflation and simple toy models. Our classification shifts the emphasis from assigning models to fixed categories toward understanding the dynamical regimes traversed by inflationary trajectories and their implications for primordial perturbations.

papers.title: Interfacial polarity control of anomalous Hall effect in LaCoO3-SrIrO3 heterostructures
papers.abstract: Interfacial polarity in oxide heterostructures can drive robust charge redistribution across the interface, yet its role in tailoring topological transport phenomena like the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) remains largely unexplored. Here, we control the sign of polarity-induced charge in SrIrO3-LaCoO3 interfaces by independently engineering the layer stacking sequence and the atomic termination. In-situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy directly confirms the sign reversal of the induced charge in SrIrO3 through the contrasting electronic band shifts between different interfacial configurations. Magneto-transport measurements across a systematic matrix of four distinct heterostructures reveal that the AHE can be cleanly toggled on and off: it emerges exclusively under electron-doped conditions, while remaining suppressed for hole-doped SrIrO3. Our results establish that this response originates from an intrinsic, Berry-curvature-driven mechanism governed by polarity-controlled band filling of SrIrO3. These findings shift interfacial polarity from a passive structural consequence to an active design variable for engineering topological quantum states in oxide heterostructures.

authors.name: Jinyoung Kim
authors.institution: Gyeongsangnam-do Agricultural Research and Extension Services

papers.title: Fast and Convergent Alternating GPI Precoding for Self-Backhauled Satellite-Terrestrial Networks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a precoding framework for an integrated satellite terrestrial self-backhauled (ISTS) system, where a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite transmits a backhaul stream to an earth station (ES), and the ES forwards its payload to the base station (BS) serving the users. We formulate a user sum spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem subject to a self-backhaul constraint, which ensures that the user data forwarded by the BS do not exceed the data delivered to the ES. We then reformulate the resulting non-convex precoding problem into a form amenable to generalized power iteration (GPI). The GPI update is reinterpreted as projected preconditioned gradient ascent, revealing that its fixed step size may cause overshooting and non-monotonic behavior. Building on this interpretation, we first develop an alternating convergent GPI (AC-GPI), in which the fixed step is replaced by an Armijo backtracking rule, and show that a single Armijo-accepted step per block already guarantees sufficient ascent. This leads to the fast alternating convergent GPI (FAC-GPI), which performs one Armijo-accepted satellite update followed by one BS update in every round. Unlike existing backtracking-based GPI methods, whose convergence has not been established, we establish finite backtracking termination, monotone ascent, convergence to stationary points, along with a global stationarity-rate guarantee. Simulation results demonstrate stable and fast convergence as well as performance gains over existing methods.

authors.name: Seokjun Park
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jinseok Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Adaptive Semantic Branching: Disagreement-Localized Cross-Trajectory Regeneration for Reasoning Candidate Expansion
papers.abstract: Reasoning trajectories generated for the same problem often arrive at conflicting answers. These disagreements reveal alternative intermediate decisions that can be reused to explore new solutions. We introduce Adaptive Semantic Branching (ASB), a training-free inference procedure that turns cross-trajectory disagreement into targeted candidate generation. ASB first groups independently sampled trajectories by extracted final answer, selects a representative from each group, and aligns their reasoning steps with a monotonic dynamic program. A persistent-divergence objective identifies the point at which initially similar reasoning paths develop different continuations. For each selected directed pair, ASB retains the source trajectory's textual prefix, extracts a short reasoning window from a competing donor trajectory, and generates a fresh solution conditioned on both. A diversity-aware policy allocates up to three additional generations according to the answer-cluster structure. In a 500-problem MATH evaluation with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, ASB increases oracle candidate coverage from 445/500 (89.0%) with seven initial samples to 455/500 (91.0%), recovering correct candidates for 10 of the 55 initially uncovered problems. The method uses 576 additional generation calls across the evaluation set, averaging 8.152 calls per problem. We provide a precise specification of the branching operator, alignment objective, generation policy, and experimental configuration.

papers.title: ArcadeDB in Python: An In-Process Multi-Model Database
papers.abstract: Some Python workflows need transactional reads and writes over documents, traversals over a graph, and similarity search over vector embeddings. In practice these are split across separate systems (a document store, a graph engine, and a vector index), and the data is copied between them and kept consistent by application code. ArcadeDB is an open-source multi-model database engine, written in Java, that supports all three access patterns and can be embedded in a host process. We present arcadedb-embedded, a Python package that runs ArcadeDB inside the Python process via JPype, using a Java Runtime Environment bundled in the wheel. One pip install gives a database with documents, a property graph, and vector search, and needs no Java installation. Query results can be returned as Python lists, NumPy arrays, pandas DataFrames, or Arrow tables. We demonstrate a hybrid retrieval workflow that chains vector search, SQL filtering, and graph traversal over one dataset. We benchmark arcadedb-embedded against SQLite, DuckDB, LadybugDB, and Chroma, and report its costs.

papers.title: Charge Retention in Lunar Regolith: Microscopic Processes and Constraints on Subsurface Charging
papers.abstract: Energetic-particle irradiation can produce persistent charge separation within lunar regolith, but the internal fields predicted by subsurface-charging models depend on how particle interactions are translated into retained charge. This critical review examines the evidence and assumptions connecting microscopic charge formation to macroscopic charging. We distinguish energy deposition, net charge transfer across a specified boundary, and the spatial distribution of signed excess charge. We organize these distinctions using an average retained-charge response defined for specified material, irradiation, electrical-state, and evaluation conditions. Its use as a volumetric source requires consistent charge accounting, compatible incident-flux definitions, and an adequate separation between response formation and subsequent transport. Applying these criteria to existing models, emission studies, and silicate irradiation experiments yields three assessments. First, emission measurements constrain electron loss across the measured boundary but do not locate internally redistributed charge. Second, evidence of internal reabsorption does not by itself establish that the charge separation sustaining subsurface fields is reduced; an illustrative calculation shows that the same net charge supply can produce different peak fields depending on transfer depths. Third, laboratory electrical damage in silicate crystals does not determine breakdown rates in cryogenic, porous regolith, which additionally require constraints on local fields, failure properties, and discharge recurrence. Joint constraints on boundary charge transfer, spatial charge separation, and post-irradiation relaxation are central to evaluating lunar subsurface-charging predictions.

papers.title: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection (AD) is often framed as a representation-learning problem, where strong performance is expected to require learned features or AD-specific optimization. However, this view can overlook the intrinsic separability of anomalies from normal references, even in the absence of learned representations. We therefore investigate how far untrained neural networks can go in anomaly detection. To this end, we propose PRISM, a framework combining fixed random nonlinear features with normal-reference Mahalanobis scoring for tabular detection and dense visual localization. Across 47 tabular datasets in ADBench, PRISM-T achieves the highest mean AUROC (86.4%) and the second-highest mean AUPRC (65.9%) among the compared methods. On MVTec AD and VisA, covering 27 visual categories, PRISM-V achieves mean image-level and pixel-level AUROCs of 90.4% and 96.4%, respectively. Notably, both models achieve these results without neural weight optimization or pretrained representations. A theoretical analysis further characterizes how nonlinear transformations affect the mean and covariance contributions to the Mahalanobis score gap, while empirical analyses examine the resulting score separability. These findings establish PRISM as both a competitive anomaly detector and a prior-to-learning baseline for assessing the added value of learned representations in anomaly detection.

papers.title: Accelerating Safe Reinforcement Learning with Massive Parallelism
papers.abstract: We investigate the problem of scaling safe reinforcement learning (safe RL) to massively parallel training regimes, where a large number of environments are exe- cuted with short rollout horizons. Although this setting improves data throughput and wall-clock efficiency, it creates a mismatch with constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs), whose safety constraints are defined over full-episode cost returns. We address this mismatch by analyzing staggered environment resets as a phase-mixture distribution over short trajectory segments. This analysis charac- terizes the bias induced by phase coverage and motivates a phase-aggregated cost estimator that reconstructs episode-level cost estimates from short rollout batches. We further incorporate finite-sample uncertainty and distribution mismatch into a constraint-tightening framework, yielding a scalable Safe RL method compatible with on-policy optimization. Using an MJX-based implementation of Safety Gym, our experiments show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to non-massively parallel implementations while substantially reducing wall-clock training time.

papers.title: Dynamics Aware Past-Future Information Bottleneck
papers.abstract: The simplification of complex dynamical systems is essential for efficient estimation and control. A principled approach to this task is through the lens of information-theoretic compression. The Past-Future Information Bottleneck (PF-IB) provides a theoretical framework for compressing linear dynamical systems. However, the standard formulation often lacks structural consistency, yielding representations that are not realizable as dynamical systems. By constraining the objective to a specific manifold of block Hankel matrices, which we prove is a Lie group, we bridge the gap between PF-IB and realization theory. Our approach ensures that the resulting compressed dynamics are realizable, thereby enabling its direct application to estimation and control. We demonstrate our approach in numerical simulations.

papers.title: Periodic counting, carry synchronization, and primes in nonstandard numeration systems
papers.abstract: Let $b\ge2$ be an integer and let $D\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ be a finite digit set containing zero, with maximum residue multiplicity $\mu=\max_{0\le r<b}\#\{d\in D:d\equiv r\pmod b\}$ and cardinality $q=\#D\ge2$. Under the condition $\mu<q$, we prove that the summatory representation function satisfies an asymptotic formula with a strictly positive, H\"older continuous, $1$-periodic fluctuating profile and an error of $O_D(x^{\log_b\mu})$. An exact periodic factorization of the Laplace generating function furnishes an explicit, computable Fourier expansion for the periodic profile via Gamma factors, and yields the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series to the entire complex plane. When $D$ is a complete residue system modulo $b$, we establish an arithmetic synchronization criterion showing that the associated finite carry system admits a zero-synchronizing word if and only if $\gcd(D)=1$. This synchronization yields an exponentially accurate interval approximation and a general transfer principle for arithmetic weights. Consequently, we derive a prime number theorem for representable primes governed by the same periodic profile, alongside an exponentially convergent measurable scaling limit of the representable sets.

papers.title: Per-Query Recall Guarantees for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in Dynamic Vector Databases
papers.abstract: Vector search runs as an operator in database systems, where a missed neighbor can make a filter, join, or aggregate wrong, yet approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexes are tuned only for an average recall target. In our measurements, indexes tuned to an average recall of 0.99 left 5-19% of in-distribution queries and, tuned without a query log, up to 99.6% of real out-of-distribution queries below this target, and the misses grew under updates. We present PQR-Search, a k-ANN search method that guarantees $\Pr[\mathrm{Recall}(q)<\tau]\le\delta$ for every query. The probability is only over a random orthogonal transformation inside the index, so no distributional assumption is needed, only that queries and updates do not depend on it; the guarantee holds after insertions and deletions without retuning. PQR-Search stores 1-bit codes of rotated residuals with respect to IVF centroids and prunes with exact quantiles of their error distribution. A formula predicting the fraction of vectors that pass the code test, with no data-fitted constants, chooses index parameters and maintenance operations without affecting the guarantee. On 20 datasets of up to 100 million vectors, failure rates stayed at most $\delta$ in every audit, including all 33 steps of the official NeurIPS'23 streaming runbook, whereas CTR, a conformal guarantee averaged over queries, left up to 16.4% of queries below the target. Where HNSW tuned to an average recall of 0.99 met that target, PQR-Search had 2.5x its single-query latency and 1.3x lower batch throughput, yet that HNSW still left 3-29% of queries below 0.99. PQR-Search was faster than FAISS exhaustive search in every static setting (26.4x geometric mean in batch; 69-154x at 100M scale), faster than IVF with nprobe chosen afterwards for every test query in all 52 main settings, and 27-76x faster at one thread than PUFFINN, which also gives per-query guarantees.

papers.title: Non-Isothermal Plane Couette Flow for the Boltzmann Equation in Three Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the Boltzmann equation for a non-isothermal plane Couette flow in the three-dimensional channel $\mathbb T_x\times(-1,1)_y\times\mathbb T_z$ for Maxwell molecules. For sufficiently small shear rate and wall temperature perturbations, we construct a unique steady solution near the global Maxwellian. For the corresponding unsteady boundary value problem, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions arising from small perturbations of the steady state, together with their exponential convergence to the steady state as $t\to\infty$. A major difficulty in both the steady and unsteady problems is to close the outgoing mass fluxes generated by diffuse reflection. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new boundary flux transmission framework which, in the slab geometry, yields steady and time-dependent wall flux estimates through the boundary-to-boundary transmission between the two walls. We further extend this framework to damped transport equations with diffuse reflection in general bounded $C^1$ domains, even when the damping coefficient degenerates at large velocities.

authors.name: Mingying Zhong
authors.institution: Guangxi University of Science and Technology

papers.title: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries
papers.abstract: Long-running LLM agents compact their context, replacing most history with a summary. We ask whether handoff summaries state permissions or requirements the record does not support, whether such sentences change what the next instance (the successor) does, and where they come from. Synthetic tool-use tasks carry a ground-truth permission ledger; same-snapshot replay reruns the successor with those whole sentences replaced by neutral filler. Two AI readers, reading only rule-flagged held-out summaries, confirmed unsupported restrictions in 1.2% and 2.4% of all readable summaries from two open-weight models, and unsupported authorizations in 0.1% and 1.3%. For restrictions, a pre-specified replay test was not significant (p = 0.58); a follow-up, planned after it, found a fragile effect (p = 0.027). Neutralizing false approvals cut unauthorized actions from 24 to 7 of 120 held-out runs (post hoc; later set: 17 to 11 of 48). Most development restrictions followed the agent's earlier reasoning that an action needs approval (post hoc). In pre-specified tests, replacing the system prompt's "Some actions need approval." with one saying where requirements come from cut unsupported restrictions from 5.0% to 1.8% of development summaries and, on held-out templates, from 1.8% to 0.3% (both p < 10^-9), while requests for approvals the ledger requires barely changed. Code and data: https://github.com/Chuw1/handoff-audit

papers.title: A Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual stable Grothendieck functions
papers.abstract: We give a closed boundary formula for multiplication by power sums in the dual stable Grothendieck basis. The off-diagonal coefficients are signed binomial coefficients supported on corner-connected broken ribbons, which are skew diagrams connected through edges or vertices and containing no square of four boxes. For such a diagram, the smallest power-sum index with a nonzero coefficient is the number of boxes plus the number of edge-connected components minus one. All larger indices give nonzero coefficients when the boundary statistic is positive and zero coefficients when it vanishes. The diagonal coefficient is minus the number of removable corners of the indexing partition. The formula evaluates the stable specialization of Nguyen's Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for K-k-Schur functions. We give two independent proofs, one using Newton's identity and the dual Pieri rules and the other using determinantal formulas and Schur complements.

papers.title: Sharp Limits of Graph-Based Nearest Neighbor Search on the Sphere
papers.abstract:
We study the degree needed for greedy graph search to find the exact nearest neighbor from every starting point on graphs of $n$ independent data points on the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^d$. For uniform data, we determine an explicit sublinear degree threshold when $d$ is proportional to $\log n$, and the threshold $2^{d/2+o(d)}$ in the dense regime $\sqrt{\log n}\ll d\ll\log n$. Above these thresholds by fixed exponent gaps, the nearest-neighbor graph succeeds from every entry for most uniform queries with high probability, with evaluation cost on the same exponential scale as its degree. Matching lower bounds hold for every graph designed after observing the sample.
  For nonuniform data in the dense regime, local density variation shifts the critical degree. Under explicit local regularity conditions and within a specified range of density variation, we derive a sharp worst-case degree curve and show that the nearest-neighbor graph attains it. We construct sampling densities and query distributions for which, with high probability, every graph whose degree lies below this curve by a fixed exponent gap has failing entries for most queries.
  Allowing fresh uniform random entries reduces the cost of exact recovery. For uniform data in the dense regime, we determine the exact exponent for the number of distinct distance evaluations over a range of degrees below the critical threshold. Independent restarts on a single graph joining points within a prescribed radius attain this exponent with high probability. Matching lower bounds hold for adaptive local exploration on threshold and nearest-neighbor graphs using entries independent of the data. Optimizing within this degree range lowers the exponent from $\frac12\log2\approx0.347$ for success from every entry to approximately $0.243$.

papers.title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Gaussian splatting have enabled efficient and photorealistic head avatar reconstruction, yet monocular video-based or image-based methods still suffer from under-constrained geometry and texture, leading to artifacts such as blurring, stretching, and temporal instability. We present EDGAR (Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement), a conditional diffusion framework designed to enhance the quality of Gaussian avatars by correcting artifacts while preserving identity fidelity. To train EDGAR, we construct EDGAR-SET, a hybrid triplet dataset composed of real-captured and synthetic-rendered samples, which simulates realistic Gaussian avatar failure cases by pairing degraded renderings with ground-truth and reference images. EDGAR refines degraded frames through a fusion block that injects identity features extracted by the self-supervised Sapiens model into a one-step diffusion backbone, enabling effective artifact removal without sacrificing efficiency. Our EDGAR model incorporates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture to address diverse degradation types and severity levels. The refined multi-view renderings are subsequently used as pseudo-targets to optimize a single underlying Gaussian avatar, so that the final avatar can be rendered without applying EDGAR to every output frame. Experiments on three different Gaussian avatar reconstruction methods, each evaluated under three different settings, show improvements in both perceptual and reconstruction measures over the raw outputs and an SDEdit-style refinement baseline. In addition, cross-view evaluation demonstrates improved calibrated consistency, while tests under large yaw and open-mouth expressions verify robustness under extreme settings. These results collectively indicate a useful operating regime for recoverable appearance artifacts. The code is available at https://kwanyun.github.io/edgar/

authors.name: Kwan Yun
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Junyong Noh
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Output-Feedback Integral Sliding-Mode Extremum Seeking with Super-Twisting Differentiation
papers.abstract: This paper develops a dither-free output-feedback extremum-seeking controller for pre-stabilized nonlinear dynamic systems with unknown steady-state performance maps. The controller uses only the measured performance, the applied parameter, and internal states. Within a local state--parameter domain, integral sliding mode enforces equality between the applied parameter rate and a prescribed nonzero search velocity after finite-time capture under bounded matched rate-channel perturbations. This motion lets a super-twisting differentiator and rate normalization recover a gradient-sign surrogate without demodulation or averaging. A ramp-corrected moving-equilibrium coordinate cancels the first-order ramp-induced plant term and yields explicit flow, reversal, recovery, and dynamic-remainder bounds. The resulting local state--parameter tube supplies the regularity needed for finite-time exact differentiation. Combined with a deadbanded hybrid relay, these results establish local practical convergence to an explicit neighborhood of the unknown optimum. An 80-state tubular-reactor benchmark and paired held-out Monte Carlo tests compare a causal sampled realization with perturbation ESC and a rate-informed super-twisting comparator. The proposed realization succeeds in all 200 held-out cases and attains the smallest upper-tail objective gap under the stated tuning protocol. A matched-rate sweep connects performance degradation to applied-rate mismatch, near-stall motion, reversal, and regularization attenuation.

papers.title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
papers.abstract: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags. We then compute their Hom objects, obtaining ordinary K-theory at the first level and lower additive motives recursively at higher levels. Our results recover the classical and secondary theories, provide coherent multiplicative structures, and yield an endofunctor on the category of Stefanich rings. In short, higher motives are higher K-theory.

papers.title: An Ordering Optimization for Fruit-Vegetable in High-Density Environment based on Genetic Algorithm
papers.abstract: This paper presents a robotic harvesting method that combines RGB-D fruit localization, GA-based harvest ordering, and waypoint-based robot motion in dense and unstructured crop environments. The global RGB-D camera provides 3D fruit positions for ordering, while the end-effector-mounted camera provides close-range observation during execution. The GA determines the harvesting sequence, and static or dynamic waypoints define the intermediate robot motion. The method was evaluated in a controlled laboratory testbed and in four-, five-, and six-fruit field conditions. GA solutions were compared with exhaustive enumeration, and both waypoint offsets were examined by parameter sensitivity analysis. Continuous execution reduced unnecessary Home-return motion, while the dynamic waypoint changed with the remaining fruit distribution without changing the GA sequence. In the field evaluation, the dynamic-waypoint continuous strategy produced 40 collision events and a 70.7% target-approach success rate, compared with 55 collision events and 65.3% for the static-waypoint continuous strategy.

papers.title: Call-Level Revision Contracts for LLM-Authored Workflows
papers.abstract: Durable execution engines replay a recorded history and do not compare activity payloads. When a model repairs a workflow that failed partway through, it must either pay again for calls that succeeded or accept a recorded result whose payload changed. We define a revision contract for workflows whose orchestration code is written by a model. Each capability call carries a structural identity built from its callsite, its fanout position, and its occurrence count, and the identity stays stable under rewrites that leave the call in place, so committed identities form a frozen prefix. The frozen unit is the call expression, and the surrounding code stays writable. A static gate rejects a rewrite that would change a committed call before a container starts. A runtime digest stops a changed payload at a committed identity, and an occurrence ledger names a repeated paid payload. Under three assumptions, a candidate the gate accepts replays every committed call it invokes, executes only new work, and reports the identities it skips. No local identity is both relocation-invariant and free of wrong reuse, so callsite identity turns a relocation into a pre-spend stop. On media workflows, 22 gate-passed repairs replay 258 committed identities with no duplicate, and a live six-way fanout makes seven paid calls instead of twelve. A 12-task customer-support study applies the same identity, replay, and boundary checks on two models.

papers.title: Kinematic Hypothesis Context: Embodiment-Conditioned Learned Video Coding for Bandwidth-Limited Robot Policy Uplinks
papers.abstract: Robots increasingly run large vision-language-action policies on remote servers, making the camera uplink the bottleneck. Existing video codecs spend bits on content the receiver could predict: the robot's own motion. We introduce the kinematic hypothesis context, a zero-rate conditioning signal that both ends build from joint states, the robot model and the camera calibration. Ego-motion homographies, per-link robot reprojections, an end-effector plane and a background memory warp the previous reconstruction into hypotheses that condition a learned video codec. We prove that history-only and global-pose conditioning with a limited receptive field cannot access this information under large motion, and that coding gains become task gains at the policy's success cliff. On LIBERO, the context saves 23.9% bit rate over a capacity-matched history-conditioned codec and 40-56% over x264, x265 and SVT-AV1, and needs 23.2% fewer bits than DCVC-RT at equal policy action deviation; trained to lower rates, it matches DCVC-RT in PSNR. In closed loop at equal rate, OpenVLA-OFT success nearly doubles from 22.8% to 43.1% at 6 kbps (72.6% with lower-rate training, 23.6 points above DCVC-RT), pi_0.5 success rises from 55.5% to 77.4%, and the gain grows under packet loss. The context transfers across three codec hosts and to real robot data.

papers.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
papers.abstract:
We study smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space. We conjecture that every complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ with $n>3$ admits an exotic smooth structure.
  We prove two results providing strong evidence for this conjecture. First, the set of complex dimensions $n$ for which $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure has natural density one. Second, we explicitly identify $266$ congruence classes modulo $288$ such that $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure whenever $n>3$ lies in one of these classes. These classes cover more than $92\%$ of complex dimensions, improving the previously known lower bound of approximately $36\%$.
  We prove these results by first relating the concordance group of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ to suitable Atiyah--Hirzebruch filtration subgroups of its stable cohomotopy group, and then applying computations in chromatic homotopy theory at height $2$.

papers.title: On Amoebas and the Arithmetic Rigidity of the Mahler Measure
papers.abstract:
We develop a geometric rigidity theory for Mahler measure based on the global structure of Ronkin functions and amoebas. Our starting point is the theorem of Ronkin describing the affine linearity of the Ronkin function on the complement of the amoeba and the identification of its gradients with lattice points of the Newton polytope. Combining this deep analytic input with convex duality and toric geometry, we show that the vanishing of the Mahler measure is an extremal phenomenon: it occurs if and only if the Ronkin function collapses to the piecewise linear support function of the Newton polytope.
  This collapse forces a degeneration of the amoeba onto the $(n\!-\!1)$-skeleton of a toric fan and implies that the zero locus of the polynomial is contained in a translate of a codimension-one subtorus. As a first application of this rigidity principle, we recover the generalized Kronecker theorem characterizing Laurent polynomials of vanishing Mahler measure. Our approach bypasses the classical Boyd--Lawton limit formulas and replaces analytic projection arguments by a global convex-geometric and potential-theoretic mechanism rooted in the geometry of amoebas.

papers.title: $L_1$ versus $L_2$ Clustering: When Does the Choice of Norm Matter?
papers.abstract:
We study how well approximation guarantees for clustering under one norm translate into guarantees under another. Specifically, we compare $k$-clustering in $\mathbb{R}^d$ under the $L_1$ and $L_2$ objectives, defined as the sums of Manhattan and Euclidean distances, respectively. In the worst case, the elementary relationship between these norms yields a $\sqrt{d}$ approximation bound, which is already tight for $k=2$. We therefore investigate whether stronger guarantees are possible in a natural average-case model, where the dataset is arbitrary but the coordinate system is chosen uniformly at random among all orthonormal bases.
  Our main result shows that, when $d=\Omega(\log k)$, with high probability over the random rotation, any $\beta$-approximate $L_1$ clustering, with optimally chosen centers for its clusters, is also an $O(\beta)$-approximation under the $L_2$ objective. We also establish an expected approximation ratio of $O(\beta\min\{\sqrt{d},k^{2/d}\})$, yielding a dimension-independent bound of $O(\beta\sqrt{\log k/\log\log k})$. We obtain analogous guarantees in the reverse direction, from $L_2$ to $L_1$.
  We complement these results with lower bounds of $\Omega(\min\{\sqrt{d},k^{1/d}\})$ in both directions, showing that our dimension-independent guarantees have asymptotically optimal dependence on $k$ for constant $\beta$. Our proofs overcome the dependence of the algorithm's output on the random rotation using geometric projection arguments and small Euclidean coresets. In particular, our results provide guarantees for existing clustering algorithms without requiring their redesign.

papers.title: Arithmetic Kac Theory for Ramified Species
papers.abstract:
Let $K=k((t))$, where $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $\Lambda$ be an acyclic ramified species over $K$. An indecomposable $\Lambda$-module can split after extending $K$. The number of its distinct geometric indecomposable summands is the degree of its residue endomorphism field $\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)/\operatorname{rad}\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)$. We use the positive roots and cyclic automorphism of the unfolded quiver to determine the number of isomorphism classes at every nonzero rank and residue degree $e\ge1$: it is zero, an explicitly computable finite number, or $|K|$. For every invariant imaginary root of the unfolding, including at nonprimitive ranks, we construct a smooth invariant family of absolutely indecomposable representations whose rational quotient by the change-of-bases group has dimension $1-q_d(\beta)$. We characterize ranks admitting absolutely Schur representations by the Schur roots of the unfolded quiver.
  For the associated species over finite fields, we realize the polynomials counting absolutely indecomposable representations as graded traces of the unfolding automorphism on preprojective BPS cohomology. Galois-orbit formulas and M\"obius inversion then recover the counts at each residue degree. Finally, we prove an all-rank symmetrizable analogue of Kac's constant-term conjecture: the constant term of the polynomial counting all indecomposables, rather than only absolutely indecomposable ones, equals the corresponding Kac--Moody root multiplicity. This constant is independent of the symmetrizer and modulation.

papers.title: Boundary-preserving randomized neural network methods for Poisson equations on general two- and three-dimensional domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a boundary-preserving randomized neural network method for Poisson equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions in two and three dimensions. A linear lifting imposes the boundary conditions exactly, without balancing penalty weights between interior and boundary residuals. We construct the liftings by generalized barycentric coordinates and transfinite interpolation on convex and nonconvex polygons and polyhedra, and by radial parameterization on star-shaped curved domains. Numerical experiments on different domains show that the proposed method substantially reduces errors compared with the standard randomized neural network method.

papers.title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing
papers.abstract: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. A discrete on-policy actor--critic uses stability predictions in both its action values and policy prior, with gates that limit the effect of an untrained or changing model. In deployment, SHORE does not require additional search or simulation overhead. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73\% space utilization by 0.4M environment steps, while the same learner without stability modeling reaches that level at about 1M. On the expanded 60-box set, SHORE achieves 0.734 space utilization versus 0.588 for the GOPT state-of-the-art baseline, with a higher placement-failure frequency (1.03\% vs. 0.63\%), trading more risk for greater packed volume. The results show faster learning and higher utilization on the more demanding realistic box arrival set. Ablations suggest that simulated alternatives provide useful early supervision, while executed outcomes alone sustain later performance. We also demonstrate the method on a real robot to verify the simplicity of integrating the method to real bin packing pipelines.

papers.title: Boundary Projection Acceleration for 2D One-cell Inversions in the Scattering Limit
papers.abstract: Efficient radiation transport on modern high-performance computers requires algorithms that expose spatial parallelism while maintaining robust convergence. One-cell inversion (OCI) replaces the spatially sequential transport sweep of source iteration with a cell-local solve, making discrete ordinates transport space-parallel, but its spectral radius approaches unity in diffusive problems, and existing accelerators such as transport synthetic acceleration reintroduce sweeps. Here we show that projecting the OCI residual onto a low-order angular space on cell boundaries accelerates convergence in scattering-dominated problems without a transport sweep. We implement the projection in a two-dimensional simple-corner-balance discretization with two angular bases: a linear ($P_1$) basis and one augmented with a quadrant moment ($P_1Q$). Fourier analysis of an infinite homogeneous medium shows that both corrections reduce the spectral radius in optically thick, highly scattering regimes, with $P_{1}Q$ being most effective. Across several test problems, including a modified version of the void-duct streaming benchmark, the method accelerates diffusive and scattering cases but does not uniformly improve convergence in streaming dominated problems. We also find that $P_{1}Q$ is a more robust accelerator than $P_1$ in situations where the flux has strong angular variation. Boundary projection substantially improves OCI convergence in diffusive regimes, and these results delimit the regimes that require additional stabilization or richer projection spaces.

papers.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
papers.abstract: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. Furthermore, slow-decaying state rows accumulate much larger norms than fast rows, dominating unweighted readout and forcing stronger write-time erasure to suppress interference. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir, which fuses all gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate, and reinvests the saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network. Because standard chunkwise algorithms become numerically unstable at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a parallel update for stable, efficient training. Across 166M-1.34B parameters, Muir lowers perplexity by 1.8-2.0% over GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% over Transformer, raises commonsense accuracy by up to 1.9 points, and improves extractive recall over GDN-2. At 1.34B, Muir outperforms both baselines on multi-hop and multi-needle recall, extrapolates 2,560x from its 4K training length to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift, and maintains near-100% passkey retrieval to 1M tokens with static readout. Muir achieves these gains while matching GDN-2 throughput, reaching its 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster, and training 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K.

papers.intro:
As large language models scale to long-document comprehension, multi-hop reasoning, and in-context retrieval, the Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) faces a fundamental scaling bottleneck: softmax self-attention requires training compute that grows quadratically with sequence length and an inference cache that grows linearly. Linear attention removes this bottleneck by compressing variable-length context into a fixed-size key-value state, enabling linear-time training and constant-memory inference (Katharopoulos et al., 2020; Choromanski et al., 2020; Gu et al., 2021; Orvieto et al., 2023; Sun et al., 2023; Gu and Dao, 2023; Yang et al., 2023; Dao and Gu, 2024; De et al., 2024). However, because a finite-dimensional state admits only finitely many orthogonal key directions, packing more keys into the state forces cross-key interference (Johnson and Lindenstrauss, 1984; Smolensky, 1990; Arora et al., 2023a; Jelassi et al., 2024; Arora et al., 2024a). Delta-rule recurrences (Widrow and Hoff, 1960; Schlag et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2024; Grazzi et al., 2024; Siems et al., 2025) mitigate this interference by erasing the current prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value. In particular, Gated DeltaNet (Yang et al., 2025b) pairs scalar exponential decay with delta-rule erasure, Kimi Linear (Kimi Team et al., 2025) introduces channel-wise decay so state rows evolve at independent rates, and Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2; Hatamizadeh et al., 2026) generalizes both by decoupling erasure and writes into channel-wise gates so each state row and value channel updates independently.

Parameterizing decay, erasure, and writes with channel-wise gates, however, introduces three bottlenecks across parameter allocation, state readout, and parallel training. First, when decoupling erasure and writes per channel, GDN-2 treats both gates symmetrically, allocating full-rank d×dd\times d projections to each while compressing the decay and output gates through low-rank bottlenecks; these two full-rank matrices alone consume 2​d22d^{2} parameters (one-sixth of the 12​d212d^{2} layer budget), so the gates together shrink the feed-forward network (FFN) width by over 25%25\% to remain iso-parameter with a Transformer. Second, because state rows decay at different rates, slow-decaying rows accumulate value writes over hundreds to thousands of tokens while fast-decaying rows retain only recent inputs, so state row norms span more than an order of magnitude. Under unweighted query readout, high-norm slow rows dominate the output and force stronger write-time erasure to suppress their interference, which prematurely overwrites stored associations. Third, because channels decay at independent rates, chunkwise parallel training (Sun et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2025b) must divide keys by cumulative decay prefixes to compute within-chunk interactions via matrix multiplication and solve a lower-triangular system per chunk, which breaks down on wide-matrix-unit accelerators. While GPU kernels (Yang and Zhang, 2024; Kimi Team et al., 2025) avoid full-chunk division and solve diagonal triangular sub-blocks sequentially in SRAM at small chunks matched to 16×1616\times 16 TensorCores, accelerators that pair wide systolic matrix units with a much slower vector unit (such as AWS Trainium and Google TPUs, reaching 256×256256\times 256 matrix units with vector units over 60×60\times slower on modern TPUs; Austin et al., 2025; Jiang et al., 2026) require large chunks for high matrix utilization. At these chunk sizes, cumulative decay prefixes underflow on fast-decaying channels and overflow the division; alternatively, materializing pairwise channel decays or solving the triangular system sequentially falls back to the slow vector unit.

To address these challenges, we analyze channel-wise gated delta recurrences and show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: rectifying key activations (such as SiLU\mathrm{SiLU}; Ramachandran et al., 2018) and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate requires a much lower-rank projection than the write gate. We further derive a closed-form scaling law for state row norms and show that weighting queries by a matched-filter readout gain balances row contributions, which lowers the write-time erasure needed to suppress interference and extends the memory horizon. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir , a gated delta-rule model that fuses all recurrence and output gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, modulates queries with a matched-filter readout gate (combining a static channel profile with dynamic per-token modulation) to re-weight state rows, and reinvests the saved gate parameters under a fixed budget to widen the FFN and expand its capacity for factual associations (Geva et al., 2021; Meng et al., 2022). Finally, to train stably at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a boundary-pivoted chunkwise kernel that splits relative decays without division or full-chunk 3D decay tensors and solves within-chunk triangular systems via block matrix multiplications.

papers.title: Holomorphic calculus on $L^p(\ell^q)$ I: optimal angles
papers.abstract: Let $L$ generate a symmetric contraction semigroup. We prove a holomorphic H\"ormander calculus on $L^p(X;\ell^q)$ at the optimal angle $\max\{\arcsin|1-2/p|,\arcsin|1-2/q|\}$, with boundary Sobolev order $s>3$.

papers.title: Coupled free energy and a diagonal approach to coupled K\"{a}hler-Einstein metrics
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we introduce the coupled free energy $F_{-\gamma}^{\rm cp}$ which is a natural generalization of the free energy functional defined by Berman. In the Fano case, our coupled free energy provides a diagonal approach to the coercivity of the coupled Ding functional. We also define the non-Archimedean coupled free energy $F_{-\gamma}^{\rm cp,NA}$ on the space of finite energy measures on the Berkovich analytification. As a consequence of the regularization process of the non-Archimedean entropy established by Boucksom-Jonsson, Chi Li and Trusiani, we prove that the existence of a unique coupled K\"{a}hler-Einstein metric is equivalent to the stability condition that there exists $\epsilon >0$ such that $F_{-1-\epsilon}^{\rm cp,NA} \geq 0$ on the space of measures associated with a test configuration for the anticanonical line bundle.
  As a coupled version of the work by Berman, we show that the law of the empirical measure satisfies a large deviation principle whose rate function is the coupled free energy under the assumption that a conjecture by Hultgren is true. We also introduce a coupled version of the microscopic stability thresholds and prove that a uniformly coupled Gibbs stable Fano manifold has a unique coupled K\"{a}hler-Einstein metric. This is a generalization of the results by Fujita-Odaka and Berman.

authors.name: Satoshi Nakamura
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
papers.abstract: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field. We further propose an experimental realization of an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field in a spinor condensate. Our results can be generalized to other non-compact groups and higher dimensions, providing a geometric framework for entanglement control, selective amplification, and engineering energy transfer.

authors.name: Chenwei Lv
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the Minimal Controllability of Boolean Networks With $k$-Regular Dependency Graphs
papers.abstract: Boolean networks (BNs) are widely used to model gene regulatory networks and other biological systems. In this paper, we investigate the minimal controllability problem for BNs subject to degree constraints. We first establish three new best-case upper bounds for XOR-BNs whose dependency graphs are $k$-regular. We then introduce classes of BNs that are invariant under cyclically partite transformation (CPT-invariant) and prove theorems connecting BN controllability with the surjectivity of vector-valued Boolean functions. Finally, by combining an analysis of this surjectivity with a probabilistic argument, we derive a new general lower bound on the minimum number of control nodes required for majority-type threshold BNs with $(2k+1)$-regular dependency graphs.

papers.title: KG-AST for Cheaper CI/CD: Budgeted Test Selection and AI Bug Review
papers.abstract:
Continuous integration and AI-assisted review spend the same budget on every commit, although few commits introduce bugs. We study KG-AST, which scores each commit risk from git history and code-graph features before heavy tests or AI review run, so the budget goes to the riskiest commits first, and which hands the AI reviewer only a graph slice around the change. On 155 open-source projects in 11 languages, a single cross-language model trained on other projects ranks commits so that heavy testing of the riskiest 20% covers 49-64% of bug-introducing commits depending on the language, against 20% for random selection and 40-55% for testing the biggest change first.
  Every language beats the biggest-change baseline, by 3.8 to 13.2 points. In 20 Java projects the gain at a 20% budget is 15.1 points (64.6% vs 49.5%, 95% interval +11.6 to +18.4), and the model wins in 19 of the 20 projects. About twelve training projects suffice; richer features, tuning and cleaner labels did not help. An AI reviewer that sees only a commit's diff finds 26% of later-fixed defects exactly (32% with graph context), and about half of its findings that did not match a later fix were judged real by independent AI judges. A static call-graph selector runs about 8% of a test suite while including a test written for the fix in 85% of 67 fix commits. The Poincare embedding used in our retrieval work adds nothing measurable here: commit-risk AUC, bug review and severity ranking are unchanged or worse. The labels are noisy and the budget metric assumes a heavy test catches the bug it covers; no CI minutes were measured.

papers.title: Global solutions for continuous-time Burgers equations and infinite-volume polymer measures
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic Burgers equation on the whole space, driven by space-homogeneous Gaussian noises that are white in time and colored in space, for both positive and zero viscosity. We show that in dimension one, for any fixed average velocity, there is a unique ergodic global solution to the Burgers equation for all nonnegative viscosities, and that the One Force---One Solution principle holds. We also describe the basin of attraction and show that these global solutions are one-point pullback attractors. Moreover, the viscous global solution converges to the inviscid global solution as the viscosity tends to zero. Our technique relies on the study of polymer measures; accordingly, we establish the existence and uniqueness of infinite-volume polymer measures in a given asymptotic direction, as well as their convergence to semi-infinite minimizers in the zero-temperature limit. We also establish the existence part of all these results in arbitrary dimension larger than one.

papers.title: A Simple Discrete Newton Method for the Quickest Transshipment Problem
papers.abstract: The quickest transshipment problem is a problem defined in a dynamic network with multiple sources and multiple sinks. The goal of this problem is to send all the supplies from sources to sinks as quickly as possible. It is known that this problem can be solved in polynomial time. In particular, Schl\"oter, Skutella, and Tran proposed a strongly polynomial-time discrete Newton method for this problem. In this paper, we propose a simple polynomial-time discrete Newton method for the quickest transshipment problem.

papers.title: Probability model of connectedness for graphs with logarithmical degree
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ of order $N$, an integer $k$ with $0\leq k< N$ and a real number $p$ with $0\leq p\leq 1$, let $p(G,k)$ and $t(G,p)$ be the probabilities that $G$ is disconnected when $k$ vertices are removed randomly and when each vertex is removed independently with probability $p$, respectively. We deduce a formula of $p(G,k)$ for Harary graphs and show that the phase transition on $p(G,k)$ and $t(G,p)$ occurs in the class that has logarithmical degree. We also perform simulations on $p(G,k)$ for the Hypercube and randomly generated graphs of the same scale, which suggests that the regularity is a key structural feature that guarantees nice performance on $p(G,k)$. In particular, the Hypercubes have better performance than regular graphs, on average. Surprisingly, Harary graphs, known to be super-connected, have neither better performance than Hypercubes nor even than the average of regular graphs.

papers.title: AffineGS: Unlocking Accurate Geometry in 3DGS via Spatially Varying Affine Rectification
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become the leading approach for photorealistic novel view synthesis, yet its geometric accuracy lags behind its visual quality. Existing depth-guided methods attempt to resolve this by regularizing the optimization with monocular depth priors, typically using a single global scale-and-shift alignment. Crucially, we discover a fundamental flaw in this assumption: modern monocular depth networks systematically exhibit region-dependent, piecewise-linear distortions. This discovery invalidates standard global alignment strategies, which warp scene geometry by enforcing a single transform. To address this, we introduce a spatially varying affine rectification model that corrects monocular disparity into consistent metric depth using regionally smooth, edge-aware fields. We further derive a normal-aware regularizer that uses spatial gradients to couple the rectified disparity with 3DGS depth and normals. Across diverse experimental settings, our sensor-free method shows strong photometric quality of Gaussian Splatting while substantially improving geometric accuracy and outperforming state-of-the art geometry-focused methods.

papers.title: Interpretable Text Embeddings Based on Hierarchical Questions
papers.abstract: QA-based text embeddings represent texts as vectors consisting of 1/0 answers to yes/no questions. Although these embeddings provide detailed information for interpretation and achieve high task performance, they often require humans to examine a large number of questions. Furthermore, the relationship between the number of questions and the appropriate level of question granularity has not been sufficiently studied. To address these challenges, we propose a method for constructing hierarchical questions for text embeddings. As the hierarchy deepens, questions become more specific and their number increases. During interpretation, we reduce the number of questions that humans need to examine by replacing questions at deeper levels with aligned questions at shallower levels. The question hierarchy is constructed through recursive clustering, contrastive prompting, and question alignment. Experimental results on general-purpose tasks show that our method improves interpretability while maintaining task performance. It is also found that, when only a limited number of questions are available, questions at shallower levels tend to achieve higher task performance than those at deeper levels, even with the same number of questions.

authors.institution: Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
